IOM repatriates over 170 Somali migrants from Libya
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
00:01:43 CST
01:01:43 KST

MOGADISHU, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- A total of 171 Somali migrants stranded in Libya returned home safely on Monday aboard a charter flight organized by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
According to the IOM, the returnees, including three minors, were stranded in Libya after surviving hazardous journeys across several countries, only to face severe hardship, exploitation and abuse at the hands of smugglers.
"Migration should never compromise a person's safety, dignity or future. By supporting voluntary returns and reintegration, the government, the European Union and IOM are enabling Somali migrants to turn a challenging chapter into an opportunity to rebuild their lives at home, in safety, with dignity, and integrated in their communities," Manuel Marques Pereira, chief of mission for IOM Somalia, said in a statement issued in Mogadishu.
Supported by the EU through the Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration in Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA) program, and in coordination with the Somali government, the charter flight first landed in Hargeisa, northern Somalia, where 42 returnees disembarked.
The remaining returnees arrived in Somalia's capital, Mogadishu, where authorities and families welcomed them before they received immediate post-arrival assistance.
Many returnees had been separated from their families and lacked access to basic services, leaving them in urgent need of humanitarian assistance and protection support.
Since August 2022, the EU-IOM partnership with the Somali government has facilitated the voluntary return of about 2,000 Somali migrants from Libya, with additional charter flights scheduled for late 2026, according to the IOM.
According to the IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), hundreds remain stranded in Libya under dangerous conditions.
Severe insecurity and a lack of necessities, including food, shelter and medical care, leave thousands in urgent need of protection and humanitarian assistance.
The MPRR-SSA initiative enables safe and voluntary returns for Somali migrants. After arrival, returnees receive housing, medical and mental health care, as well as transport to their home regions.
They later receive individualized financial assistance to help them rebuild their lives and reintegrate into local communities. ■

Finland has joined the French nuclear initiative in Europe
Kyiv • UNN
Finland has joined France’s initiative to expand nuclear deterrence through cooperation with European partners. It has already been supported by Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
Finland has joined France’s initiative to expand the scope of its nuclear deterrence through cooperation with partner countries in Europe. Reuters reports, as cited by UNN.
Details
In March, France announced the "Forward Nuclear Deterrence Initiative" in response to U.S. President Donald Trump’s concerns about the United States’ security commitments to Europe and the implications of the war in Ukraine for regional security.
"This initiative is primarily aimed at strengthening European security. It enhances Europe’s responsibility for its own defense and helps prevent escalation," Finnish President Alexander Stubb said in a post on the social network X.
Under the initiative, the exclusive right to make decisions on the use of nuclear weapons belongs to the president of France, unlike the NATO model, where a shared Nuclear Planning Group operates.
At the same time, the initiative provides for joint exercises, the possibility of temporarily stationing nuclear-capable assets on the territory of allies, as well as in-depth consultations.
Finnish Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen said in a separate statement that the agreement was a "natural step" after other Nordic countries — Norway, Sweden and Denmark — joined the initiative earlier this year.

KATHMANDU, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- Nepal's ability to monitor sudden rises in river levels suffered a major setback after the Aug. 26 flood swept away several hydrological monitoring stations, a government report said.
The report released on Sunday by the Centre for Hydrology and Water Resources Research (CHWRR) under the Water and Energy Commission Secretariat (WECS) said the loss of these stations highlights the extreme nature of the flood and poses challenges for future monitoring in the region.
The report has found that monitoring stations located at Rasuwagadhi and Syaphru Besi in Rasuwa district, Betrawati in Nuwakot and Phurke Khola in Dhading were destroyed or rendered inoperative as the flood moved rapidly through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors.
The destruction of the stations meant that water levels could no longer be continuously recorded at several critical points as the flood intensified downstream.
Seven days after the devastating flood, the Nepali authorities installed a flood monitoring system with a CCTV camera at Timure in Rasuwa to provide visual surveillance of river conditions.
According to the report, this is the first time Nepal has initiated a CCTV-based real-time river monitoring system, aimed at strengthening the country's capacity to detect sudden changes in river conditions and issue timely flood warnings. ■

====================================================================================================

Body roundness index linked to depression risk in older adults with dementia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:00:53 UTC
01:00:53 KST

New research indicates that a specific measurement of body fat distribution may help identify depression risk in older adults experiencing cognitive decline. Individuals with dementia who scored highest on the body roundness index were more than three times as likely to have depression compared to those with lower scores. The findings were published in the Journal of Health Psychology.
Dementia is a major global health concern characterized by objective cognitive deficits and functional impairment. Around 45 percent of dementia cases involve risk factors that people can theoretically modify. These modifiable risks include low educational attainment, sensory deficits, depression, and metabolic diseases.
Obesity has emerged as an especially prominent predictor of adverse cognitive outcomes in aging populations. Excess fat tissue can provoke chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation throughout the body. This persistent inflammation can disrupt normal neuronal activity and accelerate the physical deterioration of the brain.
Inflammation also increases oxidative stress and disrupts the body’s natural hormone response systems. These biological shifts are known to contribute to depressive symptoms in older populations.
Assessing body fat in older adults presents specific methodological challenges for medical professionals. The most common measurement is the body mass index, which is calculated by dividing a person’s weight by the square of their height. This traditional metric fails to distinguish between fat mass and lean muscle mass.
In older adults, muscle depletion and bone loss are common physical changes. As a result, calculating a standard body mass index might underestimate the true amount of fat tissue in a senior citizen, obscuring their actual metabolic health.
Waist circumference is another traditional metric used in medical clinics. It measures the distance around the abdomen but does not reliably indicate whether fat is sitting just beneath the skin or packed deep around the internal organs.
Clarissa Pacheco da Rocha Fernandes, a researcher at the D’Or Institute for Research and Education in Brazil, led the new investigation alongside corresponding author Felipe Kenji Sudo and their colleagues. The team wanted to evaluate alternative measurements that might better capture body fat distribution in older adults.
The researchers focused on newer metrics like the body roundness index. The body roundness index relies on a mathematical model that visualizes the human shape as an oval.
By combining a person’s height and waist circumference, the body roundness index estimates central fat accumulation more accurately than standard weight-to-height ratios. The researchers wanted to know if this specific index could predict mood disturbances in people experiencing cognitive decline.
The researchers designed an observational study involving 601 individuals aged 60 to 91. These participants were evaluated at a specialized memory clinic in Brazil between 2015 and 2024.
Medical professionals conducted standardized clinical interviews and physical examinations for every participant. They measured height, weight, and waist circumference to calculate the various body indices.
Trained neuropsychologists administered a battery of cognitive tests to assess memory, language, and executive function. Based on these standardized evaluations, 239 participants were formally diagnosed with dementia.
To measure mood, the participants completed a widely used 15-item questionnaire designed specifically to detect geriatric depression. The researchers also collected data on lifestyle habits, such as physical activity levels and alcohol consumption, alongside the participants’ medical histories.
The research team calculated several different body measurements for each person. They then ran statistical models to see if higher body fat measurements corresponded to higher rates of clinical depression.
In the total group of 601 older adults, none of the body measurements were associated with depression. The results across the general clinic population were not statistically significant.
When the researchers restricted their analysis to the 239 individuals diagnosed with dementia, they observed a distinct pattern. In this specific subgroup, the body roundness index was strongly linked to depression.
Individuals with dementia who scored in the highest quarter of the body roundness index had more than three times the odds of experiencing depression compared to those in the lowest quarter. This association remained mathematically robust even after adjusting for age, sex, education level, and general anxiety.
The models also accounted for medical conditions like hypertension, diabetes, and abnormal cholesterol levels. The body roundness index maintained its predictive power independent of these other health issues.
The traditional measurements did not perform as well in the analysis. Body mass index and waist circumference showed a non-linear relationship with depression in the dementia group.
Specifically, these traditional metrics displayed a U-shaped curve when plotted on a graph. Both the lowest and the highest measurements were associated with elevated odds of depression, which makes them less reliable as simple screening tools for mood disorders.
The researchers suspect the body roundness index performs better because it captures abdominal fat more precisely. Central adiposity is known to influence brain networks involved in attention and processing speed, which are often impaired in late-life depression.
Emerging evidence suggests that abdominal fat might alter specific genetic and molecular pathways in the brain. Obesity-related mechanisms can impair the brain’s ability to form new synaptic connections, potentially increasing a person’s vulnerability to mood disorders.
The study has a few limitations that readers should keep in mind. Because the research relied on a cross-sectional design, it represents a single snapshot in time.
This observational design cannot prove that abdominal fat causes depression in older adults with dementia. It can only demonstrate that the two conditions are present at the same time in this specific population.
The study took place at a specialized tertiary memory clinic, and the participants were all highly educated compared to the regional average. As a result, the findings might not fully represent the general population of older adults living in the wider community.
The doctors diagnosed dementia using clinical criteria and cognitive tests rather than biological markers. The study did not use brain imaging or spinal fluid analysis to confirm the specific underlying diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease or vascular dementia.
The body measurements are indirect estimates of fat tissue. They do not offer the precision of advanced imaging techniques, such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry or magnetic resonance imaging, which directly measure the volume of internal fat.
Future investigations should track patients over multiple years to see if changes in body shape precede the onset of mood disorders. Longitudinal tracking would help scientists map the exact biological pathways linking fat tissue to brain health.
Identifying depression risk is a high priority in geriatric care because mood disorders can accelerate cognitive decline in dementia patients. Simple, inexpensive screening tools like the body roundness index could eventually help doctors provide targeted preventative treatments.
The study, “Body roundness index as a predictor of depression in dementia: A cross-sectional study,” was authored by Clarissa Pacheco da Rocha Fernandes, Natalia Oliveira, Rejane Soares, Fernanda Rodrigues, Gabriel Bernardes, Raquel Quimas Molina da Costa, Naima Assuncao, Alina Teldeschi, Felippe Mendonca, Victor Calil, Andrea Silveira de Souza, Claudia Drummond, Fernanda Tovar-Moll, Paulo Mattos, and Felipe Kenji Sudo.

HKMU powers ahead with new Shenzhen Research Institute
Unknown

2026-09-14

HKMU powers ahead with new Shenzhen Research Institute
A new Shenzhen base is accelerating the University's drive for applied research and innovation
[The content of this article has been produced by our advertising partner.]
Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU) is strengthening its research footprint in the Greater Bay Area with the establishment of its Shenzhen Research Institute, a platform designed to help bridge industry, academia and research and translate research into real-world impact.
As the city’s leading university of applied sciences, HKMU has been committed to advancing research and development in recent years. Since filing its first batch of applications for research outcomes made under its auspices in 2023, HKMU has acquired or sought patents for more than 70 items. Last year, the University secured its first intellectual property licensing agreement, allowing a health-care firm based in the United Kingdom (UK) to further develop an early detection technology for prostate cancer for clinical application.
Earlier, HKMU President Prof. Paul Lam Kwan-sing emphasised that the University must focus its research efforts on specific strategic areas given its status as a self-financing institution, which came with comparatively limited resources. He called for HKMU research to be application-oriented, with the dual aim of tackling real-world problems and enhancing teaching and learning.
Strategic base on the Mainland
The first phase of the Institute, in operation since last June and officially opened in March, offers 670 square metres of wet and dry laboratory space. Plans for the second and third phases are underway and will add a further 800 square metres of laboratory space.
The Institute is currently home to a team of about 20 principal investigators and researchers from the University, as well as about 30 research and other staff members recruited by the Institute and based at there.
Turning to its research focus, Prof. Kwok says the Institute concentrates on four major areas in its early stages, with 12 projects underway: biomedical life science, net zero and environmental technologies, quantum technology, and digital fabrication and art-tech.
For example, HKMU researchers of the mangrove ecosystem have a longstanding collaboration with Shenzhen University and the administrative body of Guangdong Neilingding Island-Futian National Nature Reserve. This is the base from which the Institute will work to establish a world-class research team dedicated to both fundamental and applied studies of mangroves and coastal wetlands.
Other plans include joint explorations into optoelectronic engineering and healthcare robotics with the Zhongshan Institute of Changchun University of Science and Technology, and into wireless communications with Shenzhen Technology University.
Room for growth
The Institute was successfully registered as a public institution on the Chinese Mainland in December last year.
“This status allows the Institute to engage with different stakeholders across the country, including government, industry and tertiary institutions, to receive support for research projects and talent recruitment,” Prof. Kwok explains.
The Institute is actively applying for various Mainland research grants and funding, diversifying its research funding sources. For a start, it has obtained its first grant, of about RMB 2 million, from the Science, Technology and Innovation Bureau of Shenzhen Municipality.
Prof. Kwok believes that HKMU will benefit from the close connections between its Mainland partners and local enterprises, which could expedite the commercialisation of research outcomes and benefit society.

25 winners of math’s ‘Nobel Prize’ decry the AI invasion of their discipline
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:59:24 UTC
00:59:24 KST

Top mathematicians are increasingly pushing back against the tech industry’s artificial-intelligence-powered incursion into their field.
A statement released last Friday and signed by 25 winners of the Fields Medal, math’s highest prize, decries a “severe misalignment” between AI companies’ goals and those of the discipline. The declaration closed out what was perhaps the most consequential week in math’s history: last Tuesday OpenAI claimed a solution to the Navier-Stokes equations, one of the seven “Millennium Prize Problems,” considered the subject’s hardest open questions.
The declaration speaks to the breakneck pace of the ongoing race AI companies are engaged in as they attempt to solve the highest-profile open problems to demonstrate their models’ capabilities. The goal of mathematics is not only to solve problems, the declaration argues, but to advance the “conceptual understanding and insight” of the humans who practice it. This human culture is being endangered by the “mass production” of AI-generated proofs, it adds.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
“The mathematical community functions, in many ways, as a miniature version of humanity,” the statement says. “It consists of individuals using a wide variety of different approaches, joined by core values.”
Notable among the signatories is mathematician Terence Tao. For years, Tao has been publicly optimistic about AI’s entry on the math scene—he appeared in a promotional video from OpenAI just a few months ago—but recently his views have evolved in the direction of greater concern. On his blog last Wednesday, Tao reflected on “that infamous advertisement” with conflicted emotions. He lamented the current situation, which he said “has deteriorated markedly” and described as a landscape in which companies are “increasingly focused on the race to develop extremely powerful, autonomous AI technologies regardless of their actual value to society.”
Tao is not the only mathematical eminence with a rather sudden change of heart. Last week a number of concerned mathematicians, many of them at the top of their subject, launched the Association for Human Mathematics (AHM)—an effort that was underway even before the earth-shattering Navier-Stokes news.
“Sentiment has been building for a while now that the current relationship between math and AI companies is both harmful and short-sighted,” says Naomi Sweeting, an assistant professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and one of the first listed members of the AHM. “We’re trying to build a future that’s good for humans and good for mathematics.”
The new declaration and the AHM share the perspective that what’s happening in math should be seen as a test case, not some siloed conflict that the rest of us can ignore. “We see these as part of broader alignment issues impacting other scientific and creative professions,” the Fields medalists’ declaration reads, “as well as the whole of society.”

EU urged to beef up Arctic presence to tackle Russia 'threat'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:56:00 UTC
00:56:00 KST

A meeting of 12 European nations in Finland on Monday called on the European Union to strengthen its presence in the Arctic, a new geopolitical battleground caught between Russia and U.S. President Donald Trump.
"We call for the European Union to take on a more strategic and proactive role in the European Arctic," the countries' leaders wrote in a joint statement following a European-Arctic Summit in the town of Rovaniemi in Finnish Lapland, attended by Denmark, France, Germany, Greece and Sweden, among others.
The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc was in need of icebreakers, but it was not immediately clear if she was proposing joint acquisition or urging member states to bolster their own capacities.
Given "the situation that we are in, and considering climate change and the opening of maritime routes, we need icebreakers or ships that are able to navigate in these very difficult" conditions, Kallas told reporters.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen has suggested the EU could direct part of its ongoing surge in defense spending on a "European icebreaker capability," which is traditionally considered a civilian capability, among other equipment vital to Arctic security.
Interest in the Arctic has grown substantially since the adoption in 2021 of the EU's latest policy strategy for the region.
Trump's repeated threats to bring Greenland – a vast, autonomous Danish territory – under U.S. control have since then triggered a diplomatic crisis among Washington's allies.
While his tone has cooled since the beginning of the year, EU countries are determined to increase their presence in the region, well aware of a hostile neighbour on the other side of Finland's long eastern border.
Pointing to "the significant and long-term threat Russia poses," countries said Moscow's ambitions to increase its influence in the Arctic and its "hostility towards Europe, including the increase in hybrid activities, highlight the need to strengthen the EU's Arctic policy."
Officials present included Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Kallas and EU Council President Antonio Costa, as well as leaders from countries such as Romania and Greece.
"What happens here is not a regional story. It is a European one," Costa said.
No formal decisions were to be taken at the summit.
But it comes as the European Commission is expected to present a new Arctic strategy in a matter of weeks, which will steer the union's approach to the Arctic over the coming years.
Countries and leaders can still have a say on the final document, "so in that sense this is quite a timely meeting," Tuomas Tikkanen, senior adviser on European Affairs to Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, who initiated the summit, told Agence France-Presse (AFP).
"The idea is essentially to strengthen the EU's common strategic approach to the Arctic in this situation, where the geopolitical and economic significance of the region is growing considerably," he said.
Interest in the region has increased significantly since the EU's last Arctic policy was adopted in 2021, reflected in the number of high-level guests from non-Arctic countries in attendance.
"The security environment has changed a great deal, and there has been a lot of interest in the region recently," Tikkanen said.
Leaders discussed topics ranging from economic interests to security.
The Arctic region is warming nearly four times faster than the global average as a result of climate change, according to experts, leading to severe consequences for both the environment and local livelihoods.
As sea ice melts, countries such as Russia, China and the U.S. have been ramping up activity in the region, racing to claim natural resources and new maritime routes.
China and South Korea sent container ships to attempt to transit the Northern Sea Route in Russian waters in August, testing its viability as the passage remains free of ice longer each year.
Trump insisted earlier this year that Washington needed to control Greenland for national security reasons, though he ultimately ruled out annexing it by force.
Soon after, in an apparent move to assuage Trump, NATO launched a new mission to bolster security in the Arctic.
During a visit to the vast island on Sept. 7, von der Leyen announced a 200-million-euro ($232-million) package for Greenland, vowing to "be more present and to be more engaged in Greenland and in the Arctic."

Iranian body lists 77 vessels for violating Tehran’s Strait of Hormuz protocols
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:53:14 UTC
00:53:14 KST

Sahin Demir
14 September 2026•Update: 14 September 2026
An Iranian maritime organization has placed 77 vessels on a Non-Compliance List for violating Tehran’s protocols for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a list published by the organization.
The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) said vessels violating Iranian protocols for the strategic waterway would face restrictions on future passages, including possible fines, detention or confiscation.
The organization also warned insurance companies, protection and indemnity (P&I) clubs and classification societies against providing services to vessels on the list, citing possible consequences for dealing with them.
It urged cargo owners shipping to or from the Gulf to check the Non-Compliance List before chartering vessels to avoid potential problems.
The PGSA said any vessel working with a listed ship, including through ship-to-ship (STS) transfers or transshipment operations, would also be added to the list.
Vessels seeking removal from the list must submit a formal application providing justification, it added.
The organization did not specify in the notice the individual violations attributed to any of the 77 vessels.
The PGSA is an entity established by Iran to regulate vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Under Tehran’s transit mechanism, vessels are required to coordinate with the authority and obtain authorization before passing through the strategic waterway.
The Strait of Hormuz, located between Iran and Oman, connects the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea and is one of the world’s most important maritime routes for oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.
The waterway has been at the center of heightened regional tensions, with Tehran imposing restrictions on maritime traffic amid its conflict with the US.
The US Treasury Department sanctioned the PGSA in May, accusing it of links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and of forcing commercial vessels to pay tolls for passage through the strait.

European Commission responds to Ukraine's funding request with list of reforms

European Commission responds to Ukraine's funding request with list of reforms
A letter signed by two European Commissioners has been sent to Ruslan Stefanchuk, Speaker of the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian Parliament), ahead of the next parliamentary plenary week.
Source: European Pravda
Details: The four-page letter was signed by European Commissioner for Economy Valdis Dombrovskis and European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos. It contains several tables and a relatively lengthy descriptive section for a document of this type, which takes up two full pages.
The document does not refer to a specific funding shortfall, although President Volodymyr Zelenskyy previously said there is a "gap" of US$27 billion. European Pravda sources explain that the lack of a specific figure is due to Kyiv not having provided Brussels with a final budget calculation. This is expected to happen in the coming days this week.
However, the EU says it wants to support Ukraine. "At a time when Russia has significantly escalated its attacks, bringing yet more loss and suffering to Ukrainians, our determination to stand by Ukraine is only stronger," the letter says.
Meanwhile, the EU stresses that it expects Ukraine to demonstrate progress on reforms in return, and recalls that under the Ukraine Plan, "over €20 billion in EU financial assistance remains available for disbursement until the end of 2026, subject to the fulfilment of reforms in line with the EU requirements".
A requirement for €8 billion of this amount is the adoption of a number of laws whose drafts have already received EU approval or are undergoing assessment.
"The annex to this letter sets out several priority reforms requiring parliamentary action," the letter says.
Commissioners Dombrovskis and Kos also stressed in the letter that Ukraine should adopt these laws not only to receive the money.
Quote: "The value of these reforms goes beyond access to financing. Fairer and more effective tax and customs systems can secure resources for public services and create a better climate for Ukrainian businesses. Taken together, these reforms will further strengthen the foundations of a resilient, competitive and European Ukraine."
Details: The European Commissioners separately stressed that Ukraine must not backtrack on previously implemented commitments, citing as an example the easing of requirements concerning politically exposed persons (PEPs). The letter does not mention a possible new attack on the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO), as it was drafted before it began.
In an annex to the letter, the European Commission lists the numbers of the bills that need to be adopted.
It also stresses that the European Commission expects Ukraine to abandon the easing of PEP regulations introduced in draft law No. 15111-d. It also lists 11 reforms for which the final drafts have not yet undergone assessment by the European Commission.
Background:
- The European Commission has not yet calculated the real gap in Ukraine's 2026 budget.
- Unofficial discussions are ongoing about using frozen Russian assets for this purpose.

Europe faces an unprecedented risk of being cut off from AI technologies - Lagarde
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
18:47:58 EEST
00:47:58 KST

Europe faces an unprecedented risk of being cut off from AI technologies - Lagarde
Kyiv • UNN
Christine Lagarde said that Europe needs its own AI technologies and computing capacity for autonomy and economic efficiency. According to her, the shortage of data centers could increase sixfold.
Europe must become a producer of artificial intelligence technologies — partly in order to preserve its own autonomy and achieve the productivity gains needed to maintain its accustomed way of life. This was stated on Monday by European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde, UNN reports.
Details
European companies are investing in artificial intelligence (AI), but for the most part they import these technologies from abroad, particularly from the United States. This makes them vulnerable if access to the technologies is cut off and potentially puts every sector of the economy at risk.
"Within just a few years, AI will inspect goods at the border, determine which tax returns are subject to audit, manage train traffic, monitor patients in hospitals, and process bank payments," Lagarde said during a speech in Vienna.
"Losing access or changing the terms under which it is provided will immediately affect all sectors," she added. "This is a lever of influence that no trading partner has ever had over Europe; it can be used in any negotiations — for example, over tariffs or taxes on digital services."
Although the EU and the United States are key allies, trust between them has recently been undermined by a number of issues, such as tariffs, U.S. demands to acquire Greenland, and the withdrawal of American troops from Europe due to political differences.
The way out of this situation lies in building up Europe's own computing capacity, she said.
If implemented quickly, AI could increase productivity by 4% over the course of a decade, which would have a transformative effect on public finances, Lagarde stressed.
"Europe already has insufficient data-center capacity to meet its own needs, and according to current forecasts, this shortfall will grow more than sixfold over the course of a decade," Lagarde said.
In addition, Europe needs models that would be "good enough" to perform most tasks and operate on European infrastructure; this would eliminate the threat of being cut off from the technology, she added.
Lagarde noted that Europe is already paying for these technologies, so it should make greater efforts to master them.
The investment needs of American technology companies are so great that they are raising some of the funds in Europe, increasing borrowing costs for all other market participants and crowding them out of the debt capital market. European pension funds are also actively investing in shares of American technology companies, so any market correction would affect European savings, she added.

Immigrants express relief after Sweden Democrats suffer election setback
STOCKHOLM, Sept 14 - Immigrants in Sweden expressed relief on Monday after voters dealt the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats, whose rise helped drive the country's politics sharply to the right on immigration, their first setback in a parliamentary election.
After a nail-biting election night on Sunday, the centre-left looked likely to secure a slim majority in parliament. The Sweden Democrats lost more seats than any other party and looked set to win 17.6% of the vote, down three percentage points from four years ago.
In Rinkeby, one of Stockholm's suburbs with a large immigrant population, the centre-left bloc won 94% of the votes. One resident, 59-year-old sociologist Kahin Ahmed, who is originally from Somalia, welcomed the result.
"It's a huge relief," he said. "I think people in the suburbs turned out to vote in large numbers because they were afraid the Sweden Democrats would make things worse."
The Sweden Democrats, who in parliament have lent support to the right-wing minority government for the past four years while remaining outside the cabinet, in part campaigned on sending home larger numbers of immigrants and ending multiculturalism, with proposals such as a ban on traditional Islamic dress for women in public.
Sweden Democrat leaders blamed the loss on tactical voting for other right-wing parties and said that they had been punished for propping up the government for four years.
"That was always a risk," Richard Jomshof, a Sweden Democrat member of parliament, told Reuters. "It's part of being a bigger, more established party. It hurts like hell, but it's just part of reality that we, too, can lose votes," he said.
Silvia Kakembo, founder of the Integration Bureau, a non-partisan organisation that promotes integration, said the Sweden Democrats' efforts to expel immigrants and their proposal to withdraw already granted residence permits had gone too far, helping mobilise some voters against them.
"I interpret this to mean that many people have considered this election important, maybe even existential," she said.
The Sweden Democrats had grown steadily over decades, entering parliament for the first time in 2010 as voters balked at soaring levels of immigration. About 2.5 million people have immigrated to Sweden in the last 25 years.
Across town, in the suburb of Skarholmen, Celil Tamturk, 59, originally from Turkey, said he was very happy about the tentative result and that he had been put off by Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Akesson's comments on Islam and immigrants.
"If there were no immigrants here, after two days not working, what would happen? In schools, in healthcare, in the subway, there are immigrants everywhere," he said.
"Sweden would stop immediately."
Left-leaning parties that back the Social Democrats' leader Magdalena Andersson were projected to win 176 seats in the 349-seat parliament while Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's bloc was seen winning 173 seats, the election authority said.
Rau Amen, 70, who came from Iraq 44 years ago, said he was afraid that the Sweden Democrats were trying to create an "us versus them" mentality within the country.
"That is absolutely not what I want. Sweden has been fantastic so far, and I love Sweden. I want things to be the way they used to be," he said. REUTERS

Germany to Send 1,000 Soldiers to Lithuania, 200 Under Mandatory Assignment
Germany is preparing to conscript up to 1,000 Bundeswehr soldiers to serve with its permanent brigade in Lithuania after months of recruitment efforts failed to attract enough volunteers.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Bild on September 14, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has ordered the first compulsory assignments to begin this fall as Berlin races to fully staff the brigade on NATO’s eastern flank.
Germany plans to permanently station 4,800 soldiers in Lithuania by the end of 2027, but only around 60% of the required positions had been filled by volunteers as of August.
Bild reported that as many as 20% of the brigade could currently be affected by compulsory assignments, though the Bundeswehr hopes to reduce that share to around 10% by recruiting additional volunteers.
The military is reportedly struggling in particular to find IT specialists, logistics personnel, cooks, and enlisted troops willing to relocate to Lithuania.
Pistorius had previously insisted that the brigade should be staffed voluntarily. In June, however, he acknowledged that compulsory assignments would likely become necessary and estimated that fewer than 1,000 soldiers could ultimately be affected.
The Bundeswehr has launched extensive recruitment campaigns and even offered introductory trips to Lithuania for soldiers and their families in an effort to encourage voluntary transfers.
The brigade is expected to reach full operational strength by the end of 2027, leaving the Defense Ministry with only a limited window to settle personnel assignments. Soldiers ordered to relocate must be formally notified and can challenge the decision through legal procedures.
Earlier, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Germany’s accusations against Moscow over the attempted explosive-drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport marked the beginning of a “real war,” while also accusing Chancellor Friedrich Merz of effectively “declaring war” on Russia.

Ukraine Blasts Key S-400 Radar in Sochi, Hits Drone Launch and Command Sites
Ukrainian forces struck a radar belonging to Russia’s S-400 air defense system in Sochi, as well as drone launch facilities, command infrastructure, and other military targets across Russia and temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories on September 13 and overnight into September 14.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on September 14, the strikes included a 92N6 multifunction radar in Sochi, Krasnodar region, which forms part of Russia’s S-400 Triumf surface-to-air missile system.
The 92N6 radar is responsible for tracking aerial targets and guiding surface-to-air missiles toward them. It is one of the S-400 system’s central components for engaging aircraft, drones, and missiles.
Ukraine also struck facilities used to store, prepare, and launch attack drones near Kursk in Russia and in the temporarily occupied city of Donetsk, the General Staff said. A drone command post was also targeted in Novohrodivka in the temporarily occupied Donetsk region.
Additional Russian radar stations were hit near Litizh, Trostenchyk, and Lypovka in Russia’s Bryansk region. Ukrainian forces also targeted three Russian communications relay sites near Rokhmanove, Krasnyi Stiah, and Kamin in the same region.
In temporarily occupied Crimea, Ukrainian forces struck a short-range radio navigation system near Russia’s Saky airfield, according to the General Staff.
On September 12, Ukrainian drones struck military and industrial facilities in Taganrog and Tolyatti, including the Beriev aviation complex that services A-50 aircraft and Tu-95 strategic bombers, as well as the KuibyshevAzot chemical plant. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine later confirmed the strikes on the targets.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 14, 2026
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
23:38:47 CST
00:38:47 KST

CGTN: President Xi Jinping just concluded his trip to New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit. Can you share more details? China will take over the BRICS chairship next year. What role does China hope to play in advancing BRICS cooperation?
Guo Jiakun: From September 12 to 13, President Xi Jinping attended the 18th BRICS Summit in India upon invitation. He attended Session I and Session II of the summit, delivered important statements, and had discussions with leaders of other BRICS member states to chart the course for a new chapter of development and cooperation.
This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. President Xi Jinping summarized the course of BRICS development with three phrases: self-reliance and self-strengthening, standing together through wind and rain, and fruitful outcomes. He pointed out that over the past two decades, BRICS has been growing with strong vigor and vitality, and become the most influential cooperation platform in today’s world for emerging markets and developing countries. President Xi Jinping stressed that BRICS must stand firmly on the right side of history, and strive to be a pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development, a pioneer in upholding peace and stability, a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations, and a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, hold high the banner of multilateralism, stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy, jointly advance security governance, steer the international order in a direction that is more just and equitable, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity.
President Xi Jinping pointed out that to accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented. During the summit, President Xi Jinping proposed several initiatives, including the open source and inclusive AI initiative, the digital industry cooperation initiative, and the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative. He announced multiple practical cooperation measures, in particular, China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, establish a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation. China is committed to supporting other Global South countries in improving capacity and benefiting equally from emerging technologies so as to thrive together.
China will take over the BRICS chairship next year, and host the 19th BRICS Summit. The Chinese side will build consensus and work with all parties to plan for the future. Together, we will usher in the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, and open up a bright prospect of shared prosperity and progress.
Xinhua News Agency: On September 12, President Xi Jinping met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi while attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, extending their annual meeting arrangement into the third year. Could you talk about the new consensus the two leaders reached on China-India relations during this meeting?
Guo Jiakun: Indeed, this was President Xi and Prime Minister Modi’s third meeting in three years. The meeting in New Delhi marks the two leaders “reaffirmation” of the growth of China-India ties after guiding the bilateral relations from starting afresh in Kazan to making further improvements in Tianjin. The most important consensus reached is that China and India should be partners.
As President Xi noted, China and India have different national realities. We should draw on each other’s strengths, support each other, help each other succeed, and develop together. To promote the steady and sustained development of China-India relations, both sides need to calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic perception, help each other succeed in the spirit of win-win cooperation, remove irritants with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, and contribute to a better world with open and inclusive multilateral coordination. Prime Minister Modi said that India has an independent foreign policy, developing relations with China is not affected by any third party and that it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities on its territory. China values Prime Minister Modi’s statements.
The two leaders agreed that as the most populous countries in the world and major members of the Global South, China and India should focus on development, which is the biggest common denominator, strengthen friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation, and improve public perception of the bilateral relations. The two sides should also address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the sound and steady development of economic and trade relations. The two sides agreed to support each other in chairing BRICS, promote cooperation in the Global South, help build a multipolar world, and serve as forces for progress and stability in the volatile world. At the same time, the two leaders agreed to properly handle the disputes and disagreements between China and India to jointly safeguard peace and tranquility in the border area.
The improvement and development of China-India relations is not only welcomed by the 2.8 billion people of the two countries, but also the right thing to do to enhance the cooperation in the Global South. As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders, make the cooperation list longer, deepen people-to-people exchanges, have closer collaboration on multilateral occasions, make continued efforts to improve and grow our ties, and render firm support to each other’s development and revitalization, so that we can contribution to the peace and prosperity in the region and beyond.
Reuters: The Wall Street Journal reported over the weekend that Iran acquired satellite images of the U.S. base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three U.S. troops there in July. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on The Wall Street Journal’s report?
Guo Jiakun: China always strictly fulfills its due international obligations. We oppose exploiting the conflict to throw mud at China.
Phoenix TV: Yemen’s Houthis recently attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia, injuring more than 70 civilians and damaging multiple energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure. The Houthis said that they had also come under attack and suffered casualties. What’s China’s comment?
Guo Jiakun: China is deeply concerned about the casualties of innocent civilians and the damage to energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure caused by recent escalation in Yemen and the Red Sea. Attacks against civilian infrastructure that bears on people’s livelihoods are unacceptable. Increasing turmoil in the region serves no one’s interest. The sovereignty and security of all countries should be respected, and the only viable way forward is to resolve disputes through political and diplomatic means. China calls on the relevant parties to exercise restraint, ease tensions through communication and dialogue and work toward deescalation as soon as possible.
Reuters: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk all over the weekend called on AI companies to slow down frontier development, with Amodei arguing a Chinese advantage in AI would pose U.S. national security risks. Does the foreign ministry have any comment?
Guo Jiakun: AI is a consequential technology for the wellbeing of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only hamper efforts toward sound global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest.
Antara: At the recent BRICS Summit, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto called on BRICS member states to pursue joint industrialization, noting that each member already constitutes an important part of global supply chains. He argued that closer industrial cooperation would enable member states to generate greater added value. Does the ministry have any comment on President Prabowo’s proposal?
Guo Jiakun: For many years, BRICS has been actively promoting cooperation on industrialization, evidenced by the establishment of BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center and BRICS Center for Industrial Competences, and marked by a great number of practical outcomes. China will strengthen technological cooperation with BRICS countries, deepen industrial alignment, carry out capacity-building projects, and achieve more sustainable development featured by higher quality and greater resilience.
China News Service: It’s reported that the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Awareness Week was held in Jinan, Shandong Province today. The theme of the week is “Cybersecurity for the People, Cybersecurity by the People – Safeguarding the Smart Era with Cybersecurity.” Can you share China’s thinking for holding the event? What China believes countries should do to jointly safeguard cybersecurity in the age of intelligence?
Guo Jiakun: The internet connects households across the world. A peaceful, safe and secure, open and cooperative cyberspace is of great significance for all countries in the world. Since 2014, China has held the annual National Cybersecurity Awareness Week to improve public awareness and capability on cybersecurity, foster a healthy and positive environment in cyberspace, and provide China’s useful experience for global governance in cyberspace.
As we speak, emerging technologies, notably AI, is profoundly reshaping the cyberspace. As a firm defender of cybersecurity, China has officially put AI under the supervision of national cybersecurity laws and regulations, and has been improving relevant institutional guidelines and ethical norms. We stand ready to continue working with the rest of the world to actively respond to cybersecurity risks and challenges in the intelligence age, promote the building of a community with a shared future in cyberspace, and enable the internet to better benefit the people of all countries.
China Daily: It’s reported that some Panamanian lawmakers recently set up a so-called “Panama-Taiwan parliamentary exchange group.” U.S. lawmakers attended the launch of the group via video link. Regarding this, Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino stated that the Panamanian government reiterates that “foreign relations are directed by the Executive,” and engagements of the parliamentarians with Taiwan “do not mean that the Executive endorses them.” Do you have any comment on that?
Guo Jiakun: There is but one China in the world and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. China firmly opposes official interactions and engagements of any form between the Taiwan authorities and countries having diplomatic ties with China, and does not allow interference in China’s internal affairs by any external forces. We urge those few politicians to see the real picture. To cross the line on the Taiwan question will lead to serious consequences.
The establishment of this so-called “parliamentary exchange group” seriously violates the one-China principle upheld by Panama. We noted the statement of the Panamanian government and hopes that Panama will honor its commitment to the one-China principle with real actions to uphold the political foundation of China-Panama relations. China urges the U.S. to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, stop sending the wrong message to “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, and stop disrupting and sabotaging China-Panama relations.
Reuters: Are you able to provide an update on the status of the search mission for missing foreign nationals from the flood in Tibet and Nepal? Whether the Chinese government is in touch with Apple or other smart device makers to help locate those unaccounted for?
Guo Jiakun: We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China of the procedures for DNA information collection from relatives of the missing foreign nationals. Once the remains of any foreign national are found and after the identity is confirmed, the relevant embassy will be contacted to communicate follow-up arrangements. The Xizang Autonomous Region authorities have opened a hotline for families of the missing foreign nationals and will provide them with timely assistance.
The Paper: Not long ago, the MFA hosted events under the theme “Explore People-Centered Cities: China’s Governance, Global Engagement” in Shanghai and Jiangsu, as part of the program of the “Beyond the Capital” diplomatic tour. In the first half of this year, the MFA also hosted events under the theme “Set Sail for the 15th Five-Year Plan: China’s Growth, World’s Opportunity.” Could you share more details and China’s consideration of launching these two new programs?
Guo Jiakun: The “Beyond the Capital” diplomatic tour, a flagship program which enables diplomatic service to empower development across the country, provides a hands-on opportunity for foreign diplomats in China to have a deeper understanding of China. The events you mentioned are exactly the upgraded version of the program, with a focus on development and governance.
The trip to the Pearl River Delta helps explore the vitality of development and cooperation opportunities unleashed by the 15th Five-Year Plan. The trip to the Yangtze River Delta centers on urban governance and offers an opportunity to witness how China puts into practice its people-centered development philosophy. Participating diplomatic envoys noted that, the events serve not only as an opportunity to better understand China, but also a platform for governance experience sharing and mutual learning among countries with different cultural traditions and in different stage of development. We welcome more diplomatic envoys to join the events.
DPA: Russian news agency TASS reported that Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters in New Delhi that Indian and Chinese leaders asked detailed questions about a settlement in Ukraine and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution. Can the foreign ministry confirm this? How would China help find a solution in the ongoing war in Ukraine?
Guo Jiakun: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis has been consistent and clear. We always believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the crisis, and support all efforts for peace.

Rosatom to launch three more depleted uranium processing units
Unknown

ZELENOGORSK /Krasnoyarsk Region/, September 14. /TASS/. Rosatom may launch three more depleted uranium processing units in the medium term, President of TVEL (managing company of the state corporation’s fuel division) Natalya Nikipelova told reporters, adding that they will be based on Russian technology.
The second unit to process depleted uranium was launched at the Electrochemical Plant in Zelenogorsk in Russia’s East Siberian Krasnoyarsk Region earlier on Monday. It will enable the country to double its depleted uranium hexafluoride (DUHF) processing capacity to 20,000 tons annually.

While the current unit built using French technology was under construction, work was simultaneously underway to develop a Russian equivalent, TVEL’s head said. "We succeeded with this technology, and now we are going to scale up our own technology," she noted.

BJP stays on top, Congress gets a warning: What Rajasthan civic polls mean for 2028 assembly elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:31:46 UTC
00:31:46 KST

Civic poll results were announced for Rajasthan wards today.
NEW DELHI: The Rajasthan civic poll results have reinforced the dominance of the ruling BJP despite some setbacks, brought cheers to the AAP and the CPM, but has rung alarm bells for the Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly elections in the state.The BJP has lost some ground, but the Congress has not gained all of it. Parties like AAP and the CPM have sprung surprise in some districts at the expense of the Congress. The AAP has emerged the winner in Baran Nagar Parishad, while the CPM has gained majority in Nokha Nagar Palika.The ruling BJP led the Congress in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning over 4,179 wards against the opposition party's 3,613 as results for at least 10,200 wards were declared. Independents put up a strong performance across the state, winning 2,273 wards, emerging as a potentially decisive force in several urban bodies.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections.
This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” PM Modi wrote.
Shot in the arm for Bhajan Lal Sharma government
The results are a shot in the arm for chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma. Sharma was picked up by the BJP to lead the Rajasthan government, ignoring the claims of heavyweights like Vasundhara Raje, after the party won the 2023 assembly elections against the Congress. The BJP would be happy that despite the loss of some ground, overall it has dominated across the state.
The chief minister would especially be satisfied with the results as it comes in the backdrop of several controversies that had cropped up in the recent past. The NEET paper leak expose, the Karni Sena protest over UGC regulations and the CJP campaign against the state of government schools were some of the issues that had put the state government on the backfoot. But the results show that these issues may have had a limited impact on the party’s electoral prospects.Chief minister Bhajanlal Sharma thanked the voters for placing their trust in the party."Today, I express my sincere gratitude to the people of Rajasthan for the historic and magnificent victory achieved by the Bharatiya Janata Party in the state’s municipal body elections. I also thank all the party workers who dedicated their time and effort to secure this victory. I dedicate this triumph to them and to the people of Rajasthan, and offer them my congratulations and best wishes. The people of Rajasthan have endorsed the historic work accomplished in the state over the past two and a half years under the leadership of our Prime Minister Narendra Modi. They have embraced the Prime Minister’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ and a ‘Viksit Rajasthan,” he said.The CM also thanked the youth of Rajasthan for placing their trust in Prime Minister Narendra Modi and claimed that his government had, in the past two and a half years, fulfilled 78% of the pledges it made to the public.
Mixed bag for Congress
The Congress has also made significant gains in some key civic bodies, but the party should be worried about AAP and CPM entering the opposition space and making gains at its expense. The victory of AAP in Baran and CPM in Nokha should be warning bells for the Congress which has been the dominant challenger and only alternative to the ruling BJP.Reacting to the verdict, state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said, "When local elections happen, most votes tend to go in favour of the ruling power. This has been the trend for a long time. But this time, the BJP has been completely wiped out. In the Lok Sabha, more than 50% of their votes were there, and today they've dropped to within 34-35%.”Dostara accused the BJP of engaging in dishonest practices in the wards and delimitation.“In a major city like Jaipur, within the municipal corporation, Congress is ahead of the Bharatiya Janata Party in total votes by a margin of 10,000 votes. So, if we assess just the Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP is behind Congress by 60-65 thousand votes. The vote percentage between Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party—whenever the BJP was in power, it used to be around 9% ahead. Last time when we were in government, we were ahead by 2-2.5%. The misgovernance they've delivered, the public has shown them the mirror... In the 10 municipal corporations where the Chief Minister went, they managed a majority in only four, and that too due to dishonest delimitation; in the remaining 6, the majority is with Independents and Congress, not the Bharatiya Janata Party. This shows that this government has completely failed. Panchayat Raj elections are coming up, and in those, the Bharatiya Janata Party will face twice the debacle," the state Congress chief claimed.Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and "unfair" delimitation of wards.He said the Congress won 542 wards reserved for Scheduled Castes, against 350 won by the BJP.In SC women-reserved wards, he said the Congress won 261 seats compared with 186 by the BJP, while in ST women-reserved wards, the Congress won 53 against the BJP's 39.Dotasra said the Congress won 37 of 80 wards in Ajmer, against 32 won by the BJP.
Decisive Congress victory in Vasundhara Raje’s bastion
The Congress registered a decisive victory in the Jhalawar Municipal Council, winning 18 of its 25 wards in a region considered a political stronghold of former Rajasthan chief minister and senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje. BJP national vice president Vasundhara Raje is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan assembly constituency of Jhalawar district. The district has a total of eight urban local bodies.The Congress also delivered a major blow to the BJP in the Pali Municipal Corporation, turning the party's traditional stronghold into a closely contested political battleground.Pali is the home district of Rajasthan BJP President Madan Rathore, who has served as the party's Pali district president several times and was a two-time MLA from Sumerpur.In a significant setback for the BJP, the Congress not only emerged as the single largest party in the 65-member Municipal Corporation but also defeated the BJP in Rathore's own ward.
Boost for AAP
The AAP would be very happy with its victory in Baran. The party won 31 of the 60 wards, crossing the majority mark on its own. The Congress was a distant second with 18 wards and the BJP nine, while Independents secured two seats. The result will be a big boost for Arvind Kejriwal’s party given the fact that it has limited presence in the state.
The independents have emerged as the key players in the board formation in several districts. There are several civic bodies where the BJP and the Congress will need the support of Independent councillors to ensure control. Overall, it has been a strong show by the Independents.
The 2028 assembly elections are still over two years away and these results will form the basis for course corrections for all the key stakeholders. The BJP had won 115 seats with a vote share of 41.7%. The Congress claims that BJP’s Lok Sabha vote share fell 15 percentage points. This will be clear only after the final results and vote divisions are out.While the BJP will look to plug its weaknesses, the Congress will also go back to the drawing board and rework its strategy for the next state elections. In the 2023 assembly elections, the Congress had won 70 seats with a vote share of 39.58%. However, for now it has a bigger challenge at hand- to beat the BJP in wooing Independents where the party has emerged as the single largest party but could not gain majority.

Nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of Bihar have been affected by floods as heavy rain in recent days caused rivers already flowing above danger levels to swell further, officials said on Monday.Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.According to the Disaster Management Department, floods have affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts in Bihar.The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, along with heavy rainfall in the state, has pushed several rivers and streams above their danger marks, as cited by PTI.The Ganga was flowing at 36.19 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6.00 pm on Monday, 1.69 metres above the danger level.The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, while the Budhi Gandak had crossed the danger level at Khagaria.
The Ganga was above the danger mark at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger. The Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad and Ghaghara at Darauli were also flowing above their respective danger levels.The administration has set up 1,248 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in the flood-hit areas. Around 11,508 people have been provided accommodation, food, medical care and other essential facilities, officials said.
The Disaster Management Department said the Gandak barrage at Valmiki Nagar recorded a water discharge of 1,09,000 cusecs at 4 pm on Monday, with the flow continuing to rise.At the Kosi Barrage in Birpur, the discharge stood at 1,63,315 cusecs, against this year's highest flow of 2,55,425 cusecs recorded on July 20.Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 teams of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed across various districts for relief and rescue operations.

Meink Reveals Space Force Has ‘On-Orbit Space Control Weapons’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:28:40 UTC
00:28:40 KST

NATIONAL HARBOR, Md.—Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed Sept. 14 the Space Force has “space control weapons” on orbit today—the Pentagon’s most direct acknowledgement to date that the U.S. is operating offensive capabilities in space.
“Today, we continue to ensure we remain ready to meet the challenge of evolving threats wherever they exist,” Meink said during the opening keynote at AFA’s Air, Space and Cyber Conference. “This is why the Space Force now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.”
Meink’s explicit nod to U.S.-operated space weapons comes amid a concerted push to speak more openly about on-orbit threats and the Space Force’s ability to respond to them. China and Russia, in particular, continue to demonstrate aggressive maneuvers and are developing—and demonstrating—space weapons of their own. U.S. officials in recent years have discussed the need for “counter-space” capabilities and “space fires,” as well as the development of space-based interceptors designed to shoot down missile threats. And last December, President Donald Trump issued an executive order underlining the Space Force’s role in not only defending space assets, but also in the attack mission.
But Meink’s mention of existing on-orbit space weapons is a first. During a question and answer session following his speech, Meink said the acknowledgement was intentional and the phrasing “very well thought out.”
“It is critically important that we maintain our dominance, not only in the air but in space,” he said. “So, we’ve had to take steps to make sure that when we’re threatened, we can take care of that.”
Meink declined to discuss the capabilities in more detail during a briefing with reporters following his keynote—including whether the systems in question are kinetic or non-kinetic. He argued that while acknowledging the existence of U.S. space weapons in orbit may serve a deterrent function, “talking about the details of what we’re doing would actually not benefit that deterrence.”
“We’re not going to talk about the specifics of what we’re doing, whether we’ve tested, not tested, or anything else,” he said. “I would just say that the space environment is critical for military and economic security, and we need to make sure that the U.S. can operate freely there.”
Meink said the Space Force is working now to proliferate systems meant to help track and take out threats from space and highlighted two key efforts: the Space-Based Interceptor program and the Space-Based Air-Moving Target Indication constellation. Both are part of the Pentagon’s Golden Dome advanced missile defense shield.
On SBI, one of Golden Dome’s more ambitious technical lifts, Meink said the program has moved from “initial contract to flight-ready hardware” in under a year. The Space Force is leading a prize competition to evaluate the affordability and scalability of SBIs in increments and potentially field an initial capability by 2028.
Gen. Michael Guetlein, Golden Dome director, said in August the SBI contractor pool has completed the program’s first increment, called Gate One, which focused on solidifying a design and conducting component level testing. Guetlein said it appears all of the providers will move to Gate Two, where they will build a prototype. Those that progress to Gate Three must prove the capability works in space, and Gate Four providers must show their interceptors can be integrated with the broader Golden Dome architecture.
Another key Golden Dome contribution for the Space Force is its Space-Based AMTI program. While tracking airborne threats has long been a mission performed by aircraft, the Space Force is working with the National Reconnaissance Office to add satellites to the mix, with the goal of making the mission more resilient against adversaries’ anti-access/aerial denial systems.
The service awarded SpaceX a $4.2 billion contract in May to start building out the Space-Based AMTI constellation, and Meink said the first of those satellites will launch this month. The Space Force hasn’t disclosed how many spacecraft will initially launch or how many satellites the constellation will eventually feature.
“Taken together, these investments will help us adapt and scale the force for today and tomorrow’s threats,” Meink said.

The senior AEOI official added: "This recent destructive move by the US administration can be interpreted as nothing other than a childish behavior."

Netanyahu seeks to raise IDF budget, Lapid conditions support on canceling ‘corrupt’ haredi funds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
15:23:47 UTC
00:23:47 KST

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Yair Lapid held a security briefing on Monday, during which Netanyahu requested that the state budget be reopened to allocate additional funds to the defense establishment, according to Lapid’s office.
Lapid said he would not support the proposal if it meant raising taxes and, instead, conditioned his support for the prime minister’s proposal on canceling coalition funds being transferred “to finance haredi (ultra-Orthodox) draft evasion.”
Lapid noted that, in general, he supported transferring the funds to increase the defense establishment’s budget “because the IDF needs to be strengthened.”
“But the budgetary source cannot be raising taxes on the middle class and reservists, which is where you are leading,” Lapid added.
“Instead, include in the proposal the cancellation of the corrupt coalition funds and the tens of billions of shekels you are currently transferring to finance haredi draft evasion, and we will support the proposal in the Knesset as well.”
Adjustments can be made to the state budget if they receive the required Knesset approval.
The Knesset is currently on summer recess ahead of the October elections, but the plenum can still convene under certain circumstances. As a result, opposition support would be significant for advancing Netanyahu’s proposal.
Defense Minister Israel Katz later released a statement calling on Lapid to support additional funding for the IDF, arguing that the “economic situation is good” and that the necessary funds were available but required formal legislation in the Knesset. He stated the request was not connected to any tax increases or other budgetary items.
The defense minister also warned that Israel was “facing dramatic security challenges that require decisions to be made now.”
“The regional reality does not allow us to wait. The threats are developing, our enemies continue to act, and we must ensure that the IDF is prepared and equipped for any development,” Katz said.
“Delaying the provision of the necessary resources could have direct consequences for the IDF’s readiness and the security of Israel’s citizens,” he added.
Netanyahu’s ruling Likud party stated after the meeting that Lapid was “misleading the public about the defense budget.”
The party argued that the defense budget could be increased without raising taxes.
“Lapid’s claims are absurd and false. State revenues were higher than expected as a result of the government’s economic policies, and consequently, the deficit is also lower than expected. Under these circumstances, the defense budget can be increased without any tax increases,” the party added.
“The argument regarding coalition funds and budgets for the haredi sector is also unfounded. There have never been such amounts allocated to coalition funds and the haredi sector, and they have not even come close to those figures,” Likud stated.
Lapid’s office doubled down on its initial statements in return, responding that the Likud was “lying again and abandoning the security of the state.”
'The IDF must be given all the tools it needs to complete its missions'
His office underscored that Lapid supported transferring the funds because “the IDF must be given all the tools it needs to complete its missions.”
“Lapid stands by his demand that the budgetary source for these funds not come from raising taxes and increasing the burden on the working and serving public, but rather at the expense of the corrupt coalition funds and the billions of shekels transferred each year to finance haredi draft evasion,” the statement continued.
Prime ministerial candidate Gadi Eisenkot, who has been leading in polling among the opposition bloc seeking to oust Netanyahu, backed Lapid.
“Opposition leader Lapid is right. If the Netanyahu government wants a solution, it could meet all of the IDF’s needs until the elections, shut off the flow of coalition funds, and transfer the money from political associates and draft evaders to the IDF,” Eisenkot stated.
The 2026 state budget that was approved in March included an expenditure cap of about NIS 699 billion.
The Defense Ministry’s budget was set at nearly NIS 142b. Due to the war, the sum was said to have been increased by about NIS 32b.
The 2026 state budget also included nearly NIS 6b in coalition funds, with hundreds of millions of shekels directed to haredi institutions as part of the proposal.
