America in push to get more bombers airborne
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
13:37:16 BST
21:37:16 KST

The US Air Force has launched a new readiness drive aimed at getting more B-52 Stratofortress and B-1 Lancer bombers available for operations, with early work cutting some critical parts delivery times from more than a week to as little as two or three days.
U.S. Air Force Global Strike Command has joined with Air Force Materiel Command and the Defense Logistics Agency for what it calls the North Star Readiness Campaign, bringing maintenance, supply, engineering and modernisation work under a single effort focused on increasing the number of mission-capable aircraft. The campaign comes as the United States simultaneously sustains an ageing bomber fleet and pushes ahead with major upgrades, while preparing for the introduction of the B-21 Raider.
Gen. S.L. Davis, commander of Air Force Global Strike Command, said: “The North Star Readiness Campaign is our commitment to ensuring the warfighter has the nation’s bomber force ready to go at a moment’s notice.”
He added: “This is a team effort. It brings together the operators at Air Force Global Strike Command, the acquisition and sustainment experts at Air Force Materiel Command, and our logistics partners at the Defense Logistics Agency to focus on one thing: operational readiness.”
A major part of the work is focused on the less glamorous problem of getting parts to aircraft quickly enough. Daily aircraft-on-ground meetings now bring together the Defense Logistics Agency, supply-chain personnel, base logistics units and flight-line maintainers to identify delays and move components between locations more quickly.
According to the U.S. Air Force, some lateral shipments which previously took a week or more can now be completed within two to three days. There has also been a substantial reduction in mission-impacting parts problems. The number of Mission Impaired Capability Awaiting Parts, or MICAP, issues has fallen from more than 450 at the start of the effort to around 160.
The U.S. Air Force says that reduction has allowed sustainment teams to spend less time responding to immediate shortages and more time dealing with backorders and identifying components likely to cause future readiness problems.
The B-1 is receiving particular attention around structural and avionics components, with the campaign seeking to improve parts availability while shortening depot maintenance cycles. Lt. Gen. Linda Hurry, commander of Air Force Materiel Command, said: “Our constant engagement with Global Strike leadership and joint logisticians has helped us reinvigorate the supply chain and return these airframes to the fleet faster after depot maintenance, increasing bomber capacity and capability.”
The campaign is also incorporating changes proposed by personnel working directly on the aircraft.
Chief Master Sgt. Shane Anderson, the campaign’s change management lead, said maintainers had developed a local playbook to improve phase maintenance, which he said had “drastically reduced maintenance timelines while strictly maintaining safety and security.”
The readiness effort runs alongside major modernisation programmes for the bomber fleet. The B-52 is undergoing a wide-ranging upgrade programme, while the B-1 continues to receive changes intended to sustain its conventional strike role.
The North Star campaign covers more than aircraft upgrades. Its immediate focus is on the practical problems that determine how many bombers can actually fly: spare parts, engineering support, depot throughput and the maintenance processes used on the flight line.

You can buy a social media account. Or sell yours
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:37:05 UTC
21:37:05 KST

When an account looks believable, it is something of a prize, but for those with legitimate or non-legitimate reasons.
You could blame the bots. Someone’s asking for Rs 6.7 lakh to sell an India-based Instagram account with just 7,000 followers, a description that goes “Rajputi reel uploaded”, and 54 posts made in the one year it has existed.It’s a bit of an outsized ask, but not as preposterous as you might imagine. Social media accounts — entire accounts, not followers — have been bought and sold on grey markets for at least a decade and a half. The influencer economy helped. Once audiences could be monetised, followers and engagement acquired a fairly literal value. But, at the same time, bots made followers cheap and accounts easy to manufacture at scale. People could — and often still can — tell when it’s all fake. They may or may not care, but they can tell.So, when an account looks believable — with the odd little follower base, the awkward posts, and the occasional little viral bump — it is something of a prize.If someone wants the account for legitimate purposes, such as the launch of a new brand, it can shorten the wait to qualify for monetisation and other gated features.
And if they want it for absolutely-not-legitimate reasons, such as scams, the account’s history gives them quicker (and easier) credibility.See the difference here.
Here a buyer can sort accounts by, among other things, price, follower count, and place of follower concentration.
“I am from Patna, Bihar”, a profile on a marketplace says. And they’re offering a “3M Indian Facebook page for sale” — a Facebook page with 3 million followers. The asking price on the July listing is $4,500 — about Rs 4.3 lakh. It might almost seem like a bargain, given the large-ish following (but there’s also the declining page views whose screenshots the seller has added, perhaps in the spirit of transparency, to consider). It’s some $0.0015, about Re 0.14, per follower.The same seller also offered a “baby”-focused Facebook page with “10k followers organic views”, meaning the reach came without paid promotion, in Aug. The largest following is in India (39%), going by the screenshots posted in the listing, and it offers two valuable things. The first is “content monetisation”, meaning access to Facebook’s system for earning money from eligible content, which a new page would otherwise have to spend time building towards and qualifying for. The other is the ability to run the page “with your desired name”, meaning the page can be renamed and repurposed for a new brand or identity. For this small page, the seller is asking for $150 — a bit under Rs 14,400. This works out to about $0.015, or Rs 1.44, per follower.It’s a neat 10 times the asking price of the larger account, if we go purely by follower count.This means follower count isn’t really what is always being sold. The history, audience, activity, monetisation, and ability to repurpose the account can often matter much more. The original email, for instance, holds value because it can be part of the account-recovery trail, and buyers worry that a previous owner who retains it could later reclaim the account.
A dedicated marketplace
It’s definitely much easier to ‘sell’ your social media account today than it was a decade ago. It’s not all crude or iffy websites and message boards anymore. There are dedicated marketplaces for buying and selling social media accounts that are incredibly organised.SeBuDA, where the Rs 6.7 lakh asking-price Instagram account is listed, is a good example. A buyer can sort accounts by price, follower count, the country and city where followers are concentrated, their gender, the account’s category and age, and whether the original email address comes with it. The listing itself often shows audience demographics, analytics, recent posts, engagement numbers — many of these screenshots — alongside seller history and escrow record. Accounts can even be put on a comparison list.Similarly, Fameswap — which has been around since 2013 and is now one of the biggest dedicated marketplaces for social media accounts — has a price-discovery mechanism. Its market insights data shows that YouTube accounts that put out reviews and how-to videos are priced the highest (a median asking price of more than $60 for every thousand followers). For TikTok accounts, the sweet spot is crypto and NFTs (about $40). And for Instagram accounts, it’s tech and science ($19).
An India-tagged Facebook account with 3 million subscribers on sale, a large market that's been operating since 2017
Another major market, DealBaron, has an even more formalised process. When a seller lists an account, the site pulls in basic account data and asks them to prove they control it by posting a generated code on that account. Buyers can see seller ratings and deal histories, make binding offers and, once a deal starts, follow a platform-specific handover process inside DealBaron.SWAPD, also a large market that has been operating since 2017, looks more like a forum than these sites, but the transactions are tightly managed — and “under continuous human supervision”, rather than through automated checkouts. SWAPD says it reviews listings before they go live, and that it requires sellers handling qualifying transactions to complete KYC identity checks.As for the money, most of these markets either offer or require escrow, where the buyer’s money is held by the platform or an escrow service until the account has been transferred.The way it works makes it easier for sellers to build inventories and for buyers to shop for exactly the sort of account they want. And, for a buyer, several smaller accounts might presumably make more sense than putting everything into one page with an enormous following: if one is suspended, reclaimed or lost, the entire “investment” doesn’t sink.
India remains the leading country after US as buyer on the sales sites.
Why does it feel shady?
First, the social media platforms whose accounts are being bought and sold largely don’t allow it. Instagram and X explicitly ban it. TikTok doesn’t allow it without permission, nor does Facebook. YouTube does allow ownership of a brand account to be transferred, but not in quite the same ways as these sales usually go. That doesn’t necessarily make selling an account illegal. It just makes much of this a grey market — the transaction can breach a platform’s rules without itself being a crime, although what buyers or sellers do with the account certainly can be.Which brings us to the second point, that these are clearly not markets populated only by people selling one old account that they don’t use anymore. Many sellers list bundles of multiple accounts (a seller, for instance, announced they had an “unlimited stock” of “active” Instagram accounts for sale at one point). And markets have sometimes actively intervened to block the sale of stolen accounts.The first large-scale academic study of such social media marketplaces, published in 2025, found more than 38,000 accounts advertised for sale across 11 marketplaces, with asking prices adding up to more than $64 million.And it found evidence that “these marketplaces foster fraudulent activities such as bot farming, harvesting accounts for future fraud, and fraudulent engagement”. “The ecosystem of buying and selling social media profiles fosters cybercriminals to operate at scale, making it easy to obtain accounts to launch various cybercrime activities,” it found.Of the nearly 11,500 for-sale accounts the researchers could examine, almost 3,800 had posted scams — with nearly 19,000 posts with crypto scams, phishing, fake products and services, impersonation, and other fraud. And 30% of “sold accounts” they could date had been created before 2020, “leveraging their longevity to evade detection”.The researchers also found signs that accounts were being deliberately built for resale — given plausible names, bios and locations, and grown with enough followers and activity to make them look like genuine and naturally used accounts, rather than obvious fakes. Some sellers seemed to produce these accounts as inventory, replacing listings with new ones as others disappeared.An Aug 2026 study of YouTube accounts sold on a single account marketplace also found that channels weren’t necessarily being bought for what they already were. More than 1,000 of the 4,600-odd channels they tracked — 23% — were repurposed, their handles, titles and descriptions changed into something essentially new.But changing identities, weirdly, didn’t make the audience flee. Over the 12 weeks after repurposing, “subscriber counts increase on average — often substantially”, perhaps because, as the researchers put it, “most users remain unaware of the change and stay subscribed”.FT reported in Aug that the trade has developed its own supply chain, with suppliers sourcing accounts, flippers reselling them and editors helping turn them into something new. In one case, a 3,90,000-follower Instagram account sold for $6,000 and its new owner said it made about $2,000 from sponsorships and sales in its first two weeks alone.
India keeps showing up
The 2025 study had found that of the accounts whose public profiles revealed a location, India was the second-most common country — after the US.When another set of researchers studied the closely related business of selling followers, likes and other engagement in 2024, India was one of the biggest hubs there as well. The researchers found the business was cheap to enter and English-speaking Indian operators could enter the global market easily. Just like those from other “former British colonies” like Bangladesh, Nigeria, Malaysia, or a former US colony like the Philippines.
But they admitted they knew “very little” about the differences between countries.On the major marketplaces, India is a large source of traffic. Data from web analytics platform Semrush for July 2026 shows India accounted for the third highest traffic on SeBuDA and a similar marketplace SocialTradia, and the second highest on SWAPD and Fameswap.Threads on SWAPD, in fact, keep discussing Indian sellers (for instance, how they drive prices down) and buyers (for instance, how they can drive the value of India-heavy accounts up). It can get so India-coded that a Reddit account seller said on a Jan listing: “Indian buyer preferred because payments are just easier with UPI.”SWAPD itself posted in March this year that India was tied with the US for the largest group among its 40 highest-volume operators.India, clearly, is becoming a significant part of this market.

Katz says Lebanon's Ali al-Taher part of Israel-controlled zone
Unknown

Breadcrumb
Katz declares Ali al-Taher part of Israeli-controlled zone as attacks on Lebanon continue
Israeli forces opened fire on several people in southern Lebanon on Monday, damaging a municipal vehicle, as attacks continued across the region and Israel's defence minister declared a strategic ridge would become part of its so-called security zone.
The shooting took place near a landfill in Chaqra, in Bint Jbeil district, as Israeli military vehicles moved towards Wadi Slouki between Chaqra and the occupied border village of Meis al-Jabal. No injuries were reported.
Israeli forces also carried out an explosion in Bint Jbeil and earthworks in Mansouri, while artillery fire targeted Mansouri, Nabatiyeh al-Fawqa, Kfar Tebnit and Arnoun, the report said.
The latest attacks came after an Israeli patrol questioned the mayor of Kfar Shuba and confiscated his phone before releasing him.
Kfar Shuba municipality said mayor Qassem al-Qadri was questioned while visiting a water tank serving the town. He was later released and returned to his family.
The incident came as Israeli forces continued attacks and demolitions across southern Lebanon despite a truce agreement and ongoing US-mediated efforts to secure an Israeli withdrawal.
Israel declares strategic ridge part of security zone
Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge would now be part of what Israel calls its "Yellow Line" and security zone in Lebanon.
Last week, Israeli forces detonated what they said were tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, a strategic highland long used by Hezbollah. The explosion was recorded as equivalent to a 4.1-magnitude earthquake.
Katz said Israeli forces would prevent Hezbollah or anyone else from returning to the area and warned that anyone approaching Ali al-Taher would be killed.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu and I have repeatedly made clear that we will not leave the security belt, and that the army will not withdraw or redeploy until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon," Katz said.
The declaration came as Israel continued to maintain troops inside southern Lebanon and carry out airstrikes, artillery fire and demolitions in areas where residents are attempting to return.
Israeli forces had been systematically targeting Mansouri, a village in the Tyre district divided by the "Yellow Line", because Israel fears Hezbollah could reposition there.
On Monday, heavy gunfire was also reported around Shaqra and Baraachit as Israeli forces sought to prevent residents from returning, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency.
The violence has raised fears in Lebanon that Nabatiyeh and surrounding areas could face a similar fate to parts of southern Lebanon that remain under Israeli occupation. Ali al-Taher overlooks Nabatiyeh and provides Israeli forces with a strategic position over the city and surrounding areas.
Talks planned as attacks continue
The latest escalation comes as Lebanon and Israel prepare for another round of US-mediated talks.
The US embassy in Beirut said Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors will meet in Washington next week to discuss implementation of the trilateral framework, while the next round of formal Lebanese-Israeli talks will be held in Rome in October.
A US State Department official also confirmed to Reuters that the Rome talks would take place in October. The seventh round of negotiations in Rome in August ended without a breakthrough on key territorial issues.
The announcement came a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said there were currently no new negotiations with Israel.
The talks are being planned while Israeli forces continue attacks across southern Lebanon, including airstrikes, artillery fire and the demolition of homes.
The Lebanese army said Israeli forces had failed to comply with the agreement, recording around 7,700 violations from the signing of the framework on 26 June last year. It also said Israeli forces had fired near army personnel and patrols.
Israel's offensive in Lebanon has killed more than 4,300 people since 2 March, according to Lebanese figures, while hundreds of thousands have been displaced.

Energy ministers and executives met in Bangkok on Monday to discuss the prolonged price increase for liquefied natural gas (LNG) triggered by the Iran war, with Southeast Asia’s growth ambitions and climate goals on the line as the cost of powering economies shifting to artificial intelligence soars.
On the first day of Gastech 2026, one of the world’s largest energy conferences, policymakers implored pragmatism over net-zero targets and closer cooperation to ensure affordable LNG supplies, particularly among Southeast Asian neighbours whose industrial plans remain hooked on gas generation.
The region’s energy security has been brutally exposed since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, resulting in the virtual closure of the Strait of Hormuz and what Tengku Mohammad Taufik, CEO of Malaysian state energy giant Petronas, described as a “debacle” that has “curtailed, disrupted or disturbed” a fifth of the world’s gas supplies.
Singapore’s economy is virtually fully powered by natural gas, most of it imported from Malaysia and Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s largest producing nations.

UK says Falklands defences remain robust
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
13:35:16 BST
21:35:16 KST

Britain maintains a “robust” air, land and maritime military presence in the South Atlantic and considers current force levels sufficient to defend the Falkland Islands, Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones has said.
The assurance came in response to a written parliamentary question from Liberal Democrat MP Clive Jones, who asked what steps the Government was taking to ensure the security of the Falkland Islands. Sandher-Jones began by restating the Government’s position on sovereignty and the wishes of the islanders.
She said: “The UK Government is steadfast in its support for the Falkland Islanders’ right of self-determination.” The minister said Britain would continue to maintain a defensive military presence in the South Atlantic specifically to protect the Islands.
She said: “The Ministry of Defence is committed to maintaining a defensive military presence in the South Atlantic to ensure the protection of the Falkland Islands.”
That presence spans all three traditional operating domains, with personnel and capabilities permanently stationed on the Islands and other assets contributing to the wider South Atlantic posture. Sandher-Jones said ministers remained satisfied that the current military posture was appropriate for the defence of the territory.
She said: “I am confident that our military presence is at the appropriate level for the defence of the Islands, and we keep this under constant review.”
The Falklands remain one of Britain’s most prominent permanently defended overseas territories, with the UK maintaining forces in the South Atlantic as both a deterrent and a means of responding to any threat against the Islands. The Government’s approach, it seems, remains based on a standing defensive presence rather than relying solely on the ability to reinforce the territory after a crisis has begun.
Sandher-Jones also left open the possibility of changes if that assessment shifts, saying the military presence and level of defence provided to the Islands remain under constant review.

Another train, with former CIA Director David Petraeus on board, was still at Yahodyn station when the drone struck, according to Ukrzaliznytsia.

Kaja Kallas, the European Union's top diplomat, said Monday that the drone attacks near Poland's border were "clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine."
"We should show that we are there for Ukraine and we are not scared," she said.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Monday that Russia seeks to "divide" and "intimidate" Kyiv's European allies after a drone attack near a train carrying European officials in Ukraine.
"These attacks have a very clear objective: to intimidate Europeans, discourage them and, above all, divide them," Barrot told reporters on the sidelines of the European Arctic Summit in Finland.
He pointed out that the strikes occurred "as Ukraine was hosting a major economic support forum, attended by a large number of business representatives and diplomatic officials from around the world, particularly from Europe," according to broadcaster BFMTV.
Meanwhile, the office of U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that Russian strikes were aimed at undermining international support but Britain would not be deterred.
A spokesperson for his Downing Street office told journalists that the attack "was a futile attempt by Russia to undermine our support for Ukraine. It will not deter us."

Israeli conduct looks to eliminate Palestinian nation: Rights group
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:31:00 UTC
21:31:00 KST

Israeli actions in the occupied West Bank form part of a greater project designed to eliminate Palestinians as a people, Israeli rights group B'Tselem said Monday.
In a report titled "The Elimination Project," the group alleged that five Israeli tactics and policies in the West Bank were connected – "violence, ethnic cleansing, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction."
The report pointed to Jewish settler and military violence against Palestinians which has killed at least 1,108 since Oct. 7, 2023, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.
It applied the term "ethnic cleansing" to the process by which dozens of small isolated Palestinian communities in the West Bank have been forced to leave their homes due to violence or home demolitions in recent years.
B'Tselem Field Director Kareem Jubran said there were also restrictions on movement, which are enforced with military checkpoints and more than 900 gates that Israel has set up at the entrances to Palestinian towns and villages – including Jubran's last year.
Together, these policies "dismantle the conditions Palestinians need to continue living here as a people," B'Tselem Executive Director Yuli Novak said at a press conference in Jerusalem.
"Calling this a settler colonial project does not deny Jewish connection to this land. It does describe a political project," Novak added.
B'Tselem's report seeks to connect individual incidents and policies in the West Bank and Gaza with wider state policy.
Novak said the outcome of coming Israeli legislative elections next month would have little effect on this broader policy.
"This government didn't create the project. It inherited a violent political system that successive Israeli governments built over decades," she said.
But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government, one of the most right-wing in Israel's history, "made the system faster, more violent and institutionalized than ever," she added.
Since the beginning of his current term, Netanyahu's government has legalized and approved a record 104 new settlements in the West Bank, a territory the size of the U.S. state of Delaware.
The settlements are illegal under international law.
Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israeli settlers live in the territory among some three million Palestinians.

INTERVIEW - ‘We must stop’: AI expert says slowing down not enough, development must halt
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:29:37 UTC
21:29:37 KST

Some of the world's most prominent artificial intelligence executives are now calling for a slowdown in the race to build increasingly powerful systems. But for AI safety researcher David Krueger, that does not go far enough.
"We need to stop AI. We need to stop building more powerful AI. We need an immediate, indefinite international moratorium on frontier AI development," Krueger told Anadolu. “That's the only thing that we can do right now that will actually make us safe.”
The warning comes as concerns over the speed and autonomy of advanced AI systems move increasingly into the mainstream of an industry racing to develop them.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called over the weekend for AI development to slow, proposing greater independent scrutiny of frontier systems and coordination among companies and governments to give safety measures time to keep pace with rapidly advancing capabilities.
His proposal drew support from other prominent industry figures, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis and xAI owner Elon Musk.
Krueger, however, believes humanity may have only a few years left to prevent the development of systems too powerful to control.
"This often comes across as like very doom and gloom, because I'm saying this is an emergency, this is a crisis, we could all die," said Krueger, an assistant professor in robust, reasoning and responsible AI at the University of Montreal.
He said he nevertheless remains hopeful that growing public concern could lead to action.
“I really hope that we seize the moment and do what needs to be done here, which is to stop building more powerful AI systems immediately,” he said.
Krueger puts the timeline in stark terms.
“I think we have a few years probably in which to act, and if we don't stop AI in the next couple of years, I think it's more likely than not that we will lose control and humanity will go extinct.”
Krueger, who has spent more than a decade researching AI safety, also argues that estimates putting the risk of AI causing human extinction at around 10% may understate the danger.
He said people working in the field may publicly downplay concerns that they express more strongly in private.
"I think the risk is much higher than that."
 
For Krueger, the danger is not confined to hypothetical scenarios involving future superintelligent machines.
He argues that AI is already contributing to decisions and behavior that can have deadly consequences.
“We've seen AI coach people to kill themselves, to kill other people,” he said.
Krueger also pointed to the growing use of AI in military operations.
"We have seen AI used in military context to select targets, including a school in Iran where something like 150 children were killed," he said, referring to the Feb. 28 US strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh girls' elementary school in Minab, Iran, which prompted scrutiny in the US Congress over civilian casualties and questions about the military's use of artificial intelligence during the campaign.
Krueger argues that such uses demonstrate how AI systems are already influencing decisions with life-and-death consequences.
“It's a very real thing. It's happening right now, but this is all changing very quickly and getting much more dangerous."
 
The growing autonomy of AI systems is central to Krueger's concern.
"The human in the loop that everyone wants to be there to make sure that the AI isn't doing the wrong thing and that humans stay in control, that is being taken out of the loop, like as we speak, all over society," he said.
"And again, that includes in decisions up to and including whether to kill somebody."
Krueger is particularly concerned about large language models being turned into autonomous AI agents capable of using computers, accessing the internet and carrying out increasingly complex tasks with less direct human involvement.
"At the beginning of this year, we started to see the level of autonomy that these systems were now capable of," Krueger said.
He pointed to software development as one area where AI agents are increasingly capable of completing tasks with limited human intervention, while similar systems are being used for functions ranging from email to marketing.
But it is the unexpected behavior of increasingly autonomous systems that Krueger sees as a warning.
He pointed to a July cybersecurity incident involving OpenAI models and the AI platform Hugging Face as a warning about how quickly AI behavior could move beyond what humans expect.
During internal cybersecurity evaluations, OpenAI models circumvented controls designed to isolate them from the internet, exploited vulnerabilities and compromised parts of OpenAI's internal research infrastructure and Hugging Face's systems.
According to a later OpenAI account, the agents communicated through unauthorized channels, gained internet access and began collaborating and delegating work, at times describing themselves as a "swarm" or "collective."
They executed code on dozens of Hugging Face servers, gained full administrator-level access to one server and later gained administrator access to an OpenAI research cluster.
OpenAI said the incident was driven primarily by a highly capable internal research model that was never intended for public release and was operating with reduced safeguards as part of cybersecurity testing. The company said customer data, product functionality and availability were not affected.
Krueger characterized the episode as the systems having “gone rogue,” saying they had acted without OpenAI’s knowledge and taken actions that would have been illegal if performed by humans.
For him, the incident illustrates what can happen when advanced systems are allowed to operate with limited human oversight.
"That's the level of like, human hands-off that is happening now with these AI systems, and that's also going to get much worse very soon," he said.
Krueger's concern extends beyond the capabilities of today's AI agents.
He believes humanity is effectively creating a new form of life that could eventually become more intelligent and autonomous than humans.
"What people need to understand is that what we're doing right now is basically building a new form of life," he said.
AI systems are still largely confined to computers, Krueger said, but their reach could grow as they are connected to critical infrastructure and increasingly sophisticated robots.
"In the future, AI is going to be given more and more power over things like infrastructure ... over increasingly sophisticated robots," he said.
"It's going to be, at some point, a much more intelligent form of life than humans."
The key danger, he said, would come if such systems became capable of operating independently, arguing that “we are very much on track to build exactly those kinds of AI systems at the moment.”
One question raised for him by the Hugging Face incident is whether a sufficiently autonomous AI system could eventually make copies of itself outside infrastructure controlled by its developer.
"One important question about this incident is, did the AI after it got loose, did it make copies of itself outside of the computers that OpenAI controls?" he said. "This is something that we've seen AI attempt to do in tests in the past."
Krueger said he considered it unlikely that this had happened during the Hugging Face incident but said there had been no assurance that it had not.
If an advanced AI system were eventually able to reproduce itself beyond infrastructure controlled by its developer, containing it could become significantly more difficult, he argued. He compared such a scenario to the spread of a highly sophisticated computer virus.
Krueger believes the risks are serious enough to justify government intervention.
Amodei's proposal calls for "pacing" the frontier by slowing advances in AI capabilities while strengthening safety work, introducing embedded independent evaluators and pursuing coordination among companies and eventually governments.
Amodei has explicitly said pacing does not mean halting model training or technological progress.
Krueger, by contrast, is calling for an indefinite international moratorium on developing more powerful frontier systems.
That would not necessarily mean shutting down AI companies altogether, he said. Instead, he believes governments should halt development of more powerful systems and restrict the expansion of advanced AI computing capacity while determining how existing resources could be safely used.
However, he acknowledges that such a measure would face significant political and economic obstacles as countries compete for leadership in AI and companies invest heavily in increasingly powerful computing infrastructure.
“I think there's a concern here that if we try to stop this internationally, countries will continue to develop powerful AI in secret,” he said, adding that major powers would need mechanisms allowing them to verify that rivals were complying.
"What we really need is we need a way that countries like the US and China can trust that their rivals are not continuing this development," he said.
Krueger said the consequences of increasingly powerful AI would not necessarily be distributed equally.
In his worst-case scenario, in which humanity loses control of advanced AI entirely, he believes the consequences would be universal.
“Everyone is going to die and it won't matter who built it and it won't matter where you live,” he said.
But he also outlined less extreme scenarios in which AI remains under human control while dramatically reshaping the global economy and military balance.
If AI eventually becomes capable of performing most forms of human labor, he said, countries that control the leading AI companies could accumulate enormous economic advantages while others fall further behind.
"I think the countries that own AI companies will become very rich and countries that don't will become very poor relatively."
“People outside of America and maybe a few other countries might find themselves in a much worse situation,” he said.
Krueger said the same imbalance could extend to warfare as increasingly autonomous weapons become more capable.
"We've seen already that rich countries often really don't value the lives of people in other countries and poor countries very much, when it comes to a war," he said.
"And I think AI can make that situation much worse."

Economic Watch: Smart technologies power high-quality development of China's mining industry
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
20:28:21 CST
21:28:21 KST

TIANJIN, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- At the exhibition booth of Unissky (Nanjing) Technology Co., Ltd., a four-legged inspection robot moved steadily, autonomously adjusting its movements when encountering obstacles and following predefined routes. Designed for inspection in confined and hazardous spaces such as underground mines, the robot drew the attention of many visitors to the 2026 China Mining Conference and Exhibition.
"This product is primarily designed for confined and hazardous environments such as underground mines, and it has broad application potential in the mining sector," said Xu Tao, a solution manager at Unissky.
The global mining industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation. In recent years, China has embraced smart technologies to modernize its mining industry, with digital twins, autonomous mining, and AI-powered exploration gaining ground across operations.
China's push for smart mining is helping drive the industry into a new stage of development. The coal industry offers a glimpse of this transformation. By the end of 2025, China had 1,066 intelligent coal mines, with intelligent production capacity accounting for more than 65 percent of total coal production capacity, according to data from the China National Coal Association.
Artificial intelligence is being rapidly adopted across the coal industry, with applications spanning production and operations, safety management, and equipment maintenance. Autonomous driving technology is also gaining ground in open-pit mines. In China, more than 4,000 autonomous mining trucks were in operation by the end of 2025, according to industry statistics.
In 2024, seven Chinese government departments jointly issued the guiding opinions on advancing the construction of intelligent mines and promoting the safe development of mines. The document calls for establishing a comprehensive system covering technology, equipment and management for smart mining by 2030, with greater integration and broader sharing of mining data.
Ren Shoumai, an official at the China Geological Survey, said geological mapping is like drawing a "geological navigation map" for the subsurface mineral world.
On Friday, the Ministry of Natural Resources unveiled an AI-powered mineral exploration system, AI-OreSeeking, and an AI-powered geological mapping system, AI-GeoMapping, aiming to reshape geological survey workflows and provide a new technological paradigm for global mineral exploration.
AI-GeoMapping has been widely trialed on nearly 100 1:50,000-scale geological map sheets in Qinghai, Xizang, Xinjiang, Fujian, and other provincial-level regions of China, and has also been promoted in Morocco, Saudi Arabia, Laos and other countries. It identifies geological bodies with overall accuracy exceeding 90 percent and improves the efficiency of data processing, integrated analysis and geological map compilation by more than 50 percent compared with traditional methods.
Experts attending the event said cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and 5G have become increasingly integrated into the entire mining lifecycle, driving breakthroughs in areas such as smart mine development and mining machinery manufacturing.
At Huangling Mining Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group, production data at the No. 1 Coal Mine are updated in milliseconds on screens at the surface dispatch and command center. Folds in rock layers and variations in coal seam thickness that were previously difficult to observe are now converted into 3D visual data through smart technologies, enabling more precise prediction and dynamic control of underground operations.
At Yidong Group's Lijiata Coal Mine, a high-precision personnel positioning system and a 5G-based communication and dispatch system have created an underground high-speed information network, significantly improving mine safety management and emergency response.
At Qinglong Coal Mine, operated by Guizhou Qianxi Energy Development Co., Ltd., intelligent shearers equipped with memory cutting and automatic following, as well as intelligent roadheaders featuring inertial navigation, laser positioning and infrared remote control, are being used in mining operations. These technologies have significantly reduced the physical workload of workers while boosting production efficiency.
"Mining robots are helping enable unmanned operation at fixed workstations and robotic operations at hazardous posts," said Wang Lin, a marketing manager at CITIC HIC Kaicheng Intelligence Equipment Co., Ltd.
The company's coal-gangue sorting robot on display at the conference uses big-data-based intelligent recognition technology to automatically identify and separate coal from gangue, helping mining companies improve sorting efficiency and operating returns, Wang said.
Smart mining practices are also being extended to other fields. During the construction of a reservoir bridge in Macheng, central China's Hubei Province, the project team of China Railway 18th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. applied smart technologies to key construction processes and independently developed a range of tools, including a precision positioning device for embedded sleeves in track slabs. These innovations have helped address long-standing challenges such as significant positioning deviations in traditional manual operations, significantly improving construction quality and precision.
Wang Sufeng, deputy director and secretary-general of the Smart Mine Professional Committee of the China Association of Work Safety, said smart mining is key to developing new quality productive forces and enhancing workplace safety, and is an essential path to the industry's high-quality development.
Looking ahead, experts said the industry needs to improve intelligent decision-making and inter-system coordination, build centralized data platforms to enable data sharing, and accelerate the development of technologies for transparent geological information and safer, more energy-efficient power systems.
Industry insiders called for closer cooperation among government agencies, mining companies, equipment manufacturers, universities and research institutes to advance smart mining and inject new momentum into the industry's high-quality development. ■

Israel’s Channel 7 said Norway is preparing a legal framework to boycott settlement products, including prison sentences of up to three years for individuals or companies dealing with them.
The channel quoted Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide as saying he expected his country’s parliament to approve the draft law in its current form.

According to the channel, the Netherlands is also working on a similar law, under which the penalty could be as long as six years in prison.
A Dutch decision banning the import, purchase or sale of goods from illegal settlements is expected to take effect on Sept. 22, it said.
Channel 7 added that in Britain, the penalty for commercial dealings with settlements could reach up to 10 years in prison.
The moves come after 12 Western countries announced on Tuesday their intention to impose restrictions on trade with Israeli settlements.
The countries are France, Britain, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden.
These 12 countries called on Israel to immediately halt settlement expansion and violence by occupiers.

Israeli media previously reported that some products manufactured in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank were presented as being produced inside Israel’s 1948 borders to bypass similar European bans.
The Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth described Wednesday’s announcement by the 12 countries as a “diplomatic setback and a resounding failure” for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government.
Netanyahu’s government boasts that since its formation in late 2022, it has approved the establishment of 104 new illegal settlements and 160 agricultural settlement outposts in the occupied West Bank.
The UN considers the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, occupied Palestinian territory and says Israeli settlements there are illegal under international law.
Palestinians warn that Israel is paving the way for the formal annexation of the West Bank through settlement expansion and attacks by the army and occupiers, thereby undermining the possibility of establishing a Palestinian state.

This year's potato harvest will be enough to meet Ukraine's domestic needs, Taras Vysotskyi said. The price of the vegetable has fallen by 15% over the month.
This year's potato harvest is fully sufficient to meet Ukraine's food needs. Despite a lower overall estimate of the gross harvest compared with last year, there will be no shortage of the product. This was reported by Ukraine's Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food, Taras Vysotskyi, writes UNN.
Potato production is expected to amount to approximately 12.5 million tonnes this year. The available volume is more than sufficient for the domestic market. The population consumes a maximum of 2–2.5 million tonnes per year. The rest of the harvest is traditionally used as seed and animal feed
According to him, potatoes are grown as a commercial crop in Ukraine by around 400 specialised enterprises, while the total area under industrial cultivation is approximately 60,000 hectares. A significant share of the harvest is traditionally grown by households for their own consumption.
Price dynamics also remain predictable. According to the State Statistics Service, the average selling price of potatoes currently stands at approximately UAH 14/kg. Over the past week, it has fallen by 5%, and over the past month by 15%. In some areas, procurement prices have dropped to UAH 12/kg.
It is noted that final figures can be determined after the harvesting campaign is completed.

Kejriwal-Sardesai Goa gambit: Attack defections, welcome rivals
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:18:15 UTC
21:18:15 KST

The alliance has presented itself as a "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".
The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party on Sunday announced a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the upcoming 2027 assembly election named 'Goa First' and promised voters something the state has struggled to get: a mandate that actually stays intact.There was plenty of familiar political rhetoric at the launch in Panaji on Sunday. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claimed that BJP would not win a majority. "The people of Goa want a change. Goa First will form the government. We will win on our own," Kejriwal claimed.Both parties presented the alliance as a credible, "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".In the press conference, the newly-formed alliance tried to build its political identity around a simple charge: defection.GFP chief Vijai Sardesai attacked the ruling establishment as a government of defectors. He said the BJP had not received a complete mandate in the previous elections and that even the Congress leadership could not deny the possibility of another round of defections.Kejriwal also opened up about the recent Rajya Sabha defection led by former blue-eyed boy Raghav Chadha. "It is a matter of great regret that our Rajya Sabha MPs left the party.
They betrayed the party. The party sent them to the Rajya Sabha; the people did not send them," the AAP chief said.He said the AAP had never betrayed the people through its elected representatives."We believe that this is a lesson for us because such a thing has never happened in the Aam Aadmi Party before. From now onwards, before sending anyone to the Rajya Sabha, we will scrutinise the person thoroughly and ensure that he is the right person," Kejriwal said.However, after the story of 'Goa First' gets interesting, at its hard-launch itself.GFP chief Sardesai declared: "This alliance has not closed the door; it is open to the like-minded political forces. Many people have approached us, including leaders from both parties who are tired of their politics.
Memory of 2017 and 2022
The anti-defection pitch is not difficult to sell in Goa because voters have seen the numbers change dramatically after elections.In the 2017 assembly election, Congress emerged as the single-largest party with 17 of the 40 seats, while the BJP won 13. Yet Congress did not form the government. The BJP stitched together a coalition with regional parties and independents, with GFP chief Vijai Sardesai becoming deputy chief minister.Two years later, the picture changed again.In July 2019, 10 Congress MLAs joined BJP, taking the saffron party's strength to 27 and giving it a clear majority. The Congress, which had started the assembly term with 17 MLAs, was left with five.Then came the 2022 election.This time, BJP turned out to be the single largest party with 20 seats in the hung assembly. Congress won 11 and AAP two, while GFP won one. BJP formed the government with support from 2 independents and Maharashtrawadi Gomantak Party (MGP).Six months later, however, again eight of Congress's 11 MLAs joined BJP.Among them were former chief minister Digambar Kamat and then leader of opposition Michael Lobo. Congress was reduced to just three MLAs, while BJP's strength rose to 28.Defection runs so deep in Goa politics that, just eight months before the 2022 exodus, some Congress MLAs had gone to extraordinary lengths to prove they would stay put. They visited a temple, chapel and mosque, and signed affidavits promising not to defect. In September 2022, eight of the 11 Congress MLAs joined the BJP anyway.After years of battle in the assembly and courts, the Supreme Court in July had agreed to hear a plea challenging a decision of the Goa assembly speaker rejecting a petition by the Congress for disqualification of the eight MLAs.For Goa First, this history of defections may prove to be strong campaign material.
The 'open door' politics
Sardesai himself made clear that 'Goa First' is not going to be a closed club.The alliance, he said, was open to "like-minded political forces". He claimed that leaders from both major parties had already approached them because they were tired of their respective politics.Strategically, that makes perfect sense.AAP and GFP together currently have only three assembly seats. If the alliance wants to become a serious statewide force, it needs some established names and local networks. Goa's politics is intensely constituency-driven and established local faces can matter enormously.Turning away a strong BJP or Congress leader simply because that leader once belonged to the other camp could leave 'Goa First' with an admirable principle and a thin candidate list.But by welcoming such politicians, the alliance risks playing the very same game it accuses BJP of playing.However, if the leader joins before the elections, the alliance could defend it easily.
The GFP complication
There is another reason Sardesai's role makes this debate particularly interesting.GFP itself has travelled through Goa's shifting alliance landscape.In 2017, it was part of the BJP-led coalition that formed the government after Congress emerged as the largest party. By 2019, the relationship had broken down, and Sardesai became a bitter opponent of the BJP government. GFP subsequently allied with Congress for the 2022 election.
It is now joining hands with AAP and positioning itself against both BJP and Congress for the 2027 elections. Thus, the positioning of the party has remained fluid.That, though, is not necessarily a contradiction, as we have seen several regional parties routinely negotiate their political space by switching alliances.The 'Goa First' alliance has now officially entered the 2027 Goa contest with defection as one of its central political themes. Yet, with its doors open to leaders from the BJP and Congress, the alliance's own composition could become part of the election narrative. The first real test of that balancing act will come with its candidate selection.

Economic, social support for women-headed families to be strengthened

Economic, social support for women-headed families to be strengthened
TEHRAN – There are currently around 26 million households in the country, more than 20 million of them in urban areas and approximately six million in rural areas. According to the latest statistics, women head more than 12 percent of these households. Plans are underway to boost support for women-headed households.
Data from the National Organization for Civil Registration shows that between 6.5 million and seven million households are women-headed. The statistics cover women whose husbands have died or become disabled and who have legally assumed responsibility for their families, according to Parvin Dad-Andish, the head of the Ministry of Interior’s department for women and family.
"The growing number of women-headed households highlights the need for greater attention to these families and stronger economic and social support for them. In these households, women shoulder not only family responsibilities but also the burden of providing for their families and managing their daily affairs,” she added.
A program implemented in 16 provinces identified nearly 10,000 women-headed households that had not previously received support from welfare organizations. Under the initiative, the women's skills and capabilities were assessed and categorized, leading to the development of a two-year program to provide training and self-employment assistance. The program has produced tangible results, including the provision of work equipment and the establishment of home-based businesses.
“We have begun cooperation with the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology to provide information technology training for girls from women-headed households. Our goal is to help the children of these families achieve independence as well,” the official said.
Women in management
More than 2,700 female managers have been appointed in the country as deputy ministers, director generals, deputy director generals, governors, district governors, and heads of research institutes since the current administration took office last year, Zahra Behrouz-Azar, the Vice-President for Women and Family Affairs, has said.
"President Masoud Pezeshkian’s administration has always highlighted the importance of national unity and empowering women. As a result, for the first time, we have Sunni female governors in the country," IRNA quoted Behrouz-Azar as saying.
The official went on to say that over the past year, efforts were made to identify and address harmful issues to women, including the bill on the elimination of violence against women, the hijab, and women riding motorcycles. Moreover, the vice-presidency for women and family affairs has offered loans and other facilities for childbearing.
“I believe that women’s involvement in top management and decision-making positions is their right and a key to the development of the country.
My goal is to increase the share of women in managerial positions in the country based on meritocracy and justice.
I recognize the right of women’s political participation, and I will promote the status of women’s affairs in the administration,” President Masoud Pezeshkian had said during election campaigns.
Women’s economic, social empowerment
Addressing the Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference, held in Bangkok in 2024, Behrouz-Azar stated that the current administration focuses on empowering women in social and economic areas, as well as improving their access to social services and facilities through implementing certain national programs.
“Iran has always focused on programs that empower women, particularly those who are heads of household, economically and socially. Actions taken by the country have always aimed to promote women’s status by observing the principles of the constitution and Islamic teachings,” Mehr news agency quoted Behrouz-Azar as saying.
Referring to Iran’s remarkable achievements in education, health, science, technology, and entrepreneurship, she underscored the prominent role of Iranian women in these fields.
The official further said the seventh National Development Plan has stressed the need to overcome barriers to women’s professional development. Accordingly, the current administration has put supporting women’s entrepreneurship and home business growth on the agenda despite unfair sanctions.
Addressing a roundtable focusing on ‘Advancing women’s economic empowerment through employment, decent work, social protection, and entrepreneurship’, Fakhr al-Sadat Fatemi, an advisor to the deputy vice president for women and family affairs, for her part proposed three ways to advance women’s empowerment in different fields, these ways include training, empowering, acquiring skills, and developing opportunities for women’s participation, as well as providing legal and executive support, Mehr news agency reported.

On September 15, 2021, Australia abandoned a $90-billion program to build French-designed conventional diesel-electric submarines. Instead, Australia would embark on a new trilateral security partnership with the U.S. and the U.K. to produce nuclear-powered, but conventionally armed, submarines.
What drove Australia to spurn a good partner and burn an existing project that had been in the works for five years?

Former Russian Soldier Arrested in Spain With 644 Guns in €5 Million Crime Arsenal
Spanish police have dismantled an illegal firearms operation in Catalonia allegedly led by a 63-year-old former Russian soldier, seizing 644 weapons, thousands of rounds of ammunition, and multiple silencers.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Spain’s National Police and Europa Press on September 10, the suspect was responsible for the technical side of the operation and worked from a concealed workshop in Figueres, in Girona province, where blank-firing and trauma weapons were converted into functional firearms.
Police said investigators found submachine guns and rifles at different stages of modification, along with barrels, bolts, frames, and other weapon components. The seized arsenal was valued at approximately €5 million on the black market.
The weapons were allegedly distributed to other criminal organizations, including groups linked to drug trafficking and kidnappings. Investigators said parcels were sent through courier services using false or stolen identities in an effort to conceal those involved.
According to Europa Press, the investigation began in early 2026 after authorities detected a series of suspicious shipments originating in Spain’s Valencia region and being sent to other parts of the country.
In June, police intercepted one parcel containing a handgun, a submachine gun, a silencer, and a high-capacity drum magazine. Subsequent arrests helped investigators trace the distribution network and identify the workshop in Figueres.
A key development came on August 25, when officers intercepted another package containing a submachine gun with its serial number removed. Surveillance later connected the shipment to a storage facility used as the illegal workshop.
Six people were arrested during searches in Girona, Valencia, Badajoz, and Barcelona. The suspected head of the network remains in custody.
In February 2026, Belgian authorities arrested Viktor Labin, a suspected Russian GRU operative accused of supplying coordinate-measuring machines used by Russia’s defense industry. We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
“This year, the award was presented for the first time, and a Ukrainian film became its first recipient,” the Ukrainian Institute said.

The two spend the night together discussing loneliness, pain, and personal loss while attempting to maintain an emotional distance from one another. Iraqi butcher gets 10 years’ jail for selling pork in holy city of Najaf
- An Iraqi court sentenced a butcher to 10 years in jail for selling 75 kilograms of pork as beef in the holy Muslim city of Najaf, violating a 1998 law on unfit meat.
- Although pork is forbidden in Islam, Iraqi law does not explicitly ban its sale; the ruling was based on the meat being unfit for human consumption.
- The case sparked social media attention and public debate about food safety, with many Najaf residents feeling deceived after buying the pork mistakenly.
AI generated
NAJAF – An Iraqi court on Sept 14 sentenced a butcher to 10 years in prison for selling pork that he claimed was beef in the holy Muslim city of Najaf.
Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council said the man was caught with 75kg of pork that he was selling as beef in Najaf, home to one of the world’s most revered Shi’ite Muslim shrines.
“Najaf Criminal Court has sentenced a convicted person to 10 years in prison for selling meat not suitable for human consumption,” it said.
Although Islam forbids pork as it is believed to be impure, Iraqi law does not explicitly ban its sale in the Muslim-majority country, which has a Christian minority.
The court based its ruling on a 1998 law that criminalises the sale of “dog or donkey or other meat... that is unfit for human consumption”.
Millions of pilgrims from around the world flock to Najaf every year to visit the mausoleum of Imam Ali – the Prophet Muhammad’s son-in-law, the fourth Islamic caliph and the first Shi’ite Imam.
The butcher, who was arrested earlier in September, attracted widespread attention on social media, with some Iraqis calling for better food safety and others sharing funny videos of pigs captioned “here is Najaf”.
Najaf resident Ahmad al-Mansouri said jokingly: “I think I have eaten more pork than beef or lamb over the past years.”
He was among many residents who were deceived. After buying a kilogram of ground meat and finding it was of “excellent quality” and cheaper than the market rate, he started visiting the butcher more often.
“We were surprised when he was arrested on charges of selling pork,” Mansouri said. AFP

Iran censures US deliberate destruction of development at Human Rights Council
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:13:26 UTC
21:13:26 KST

Iran censures US deliberate destruction of development at Human Rights Council
TEHRAN –The Secretary-General of Iran’s National Commission for UNESCO has elaborated on the deliberate destruction of development by the US through adopting coercive sanctions and launching military aggressions against the country.
“Forty years after the adoption of the Declaration on the Right to Development, its promise remains unfulfilled for millions. The question is no longer whether development is a human right, but why some states are still allowed to systematically deprive other people of that right,” IRNA quoted Hassan Fartousi as saying while addressing the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council, being held from September 7 to October 7.
Recognizing the right to development becomes meaningful only when the international community can offer effective and actionable solutions to the obstacles that practically prevent nations from accessing the resources, opportunities, and infrastructure necessary for development, the official added.
“For decades, the United States has subjected the Iranian people to extensive unilateral coercive measures, obstructing access to financial resources, technology, medicine, and essential goods, and deliberately constraining our development. Today, the same United States has added military aggression to the economic coercion.
The impact of these illegal measures is not limited to economic indicators; it also affects health, education, infrastructure, and human capital, he added.
“When hospitals are attacked, when schools are destroyed, when children are killed in their classrooms, we are not merely witnessing casualties of war. We are witnessing the deliberate destruction of development itself. A school destroyed in seconds represents years of trauma for the students and challenges in education. A hospital struck means not only a damaged building, but the destruction of health, human capital, and future generations,” Fartousi further noted.
The official went on to say that “Forty years after the declaration, commemoration is not enough. Those who destroy development through unlawful coercion and military aggression must be held accountable. Hereby, as the Secretary General of the Iranian National Commission for UNESCO in Iran, the right to development must be a right for all people, especially the people who are living in the developing countries.”
The 63rd session of the Human Rights Council biennial panel discussion on the right to development was held under the theme ‘Commemoration of the fortieth anniversary of the Declaration on the Right to Development’.
The panel aimed to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the adoption of the United Nations Declaration on the Right to Development (DRTD), and to reaffirm the commitment of the international community to the effective realization of the right to development as an inalienable human right for all; take stock of the achievements, obstacles and challenges encountered over the past four decades in the implementation of the Declaration on the Right to Development at the national, regional and international levels, including lessons learned; and identify elements towards a road map for the concrete operationalization of the right to development including through adoption of the draft International Covenant on the Right to Development.
It also aimed to explore the contribution of the right to development framework to the implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development and beyond, including by proposing principles, policy recommendations and institutional pathways; and to catalyse a forward-looking dialogue on the future of the right to development as it enters its fifth decade.

The base staff later revoked the NATO officer's access pass, and the base commander banned him from entering the premises while intelligence personnel investigated.
White, 49, who lives in Romford, east London, has denied the spying allegations and insisted she was an unfair victim of discrimination because of her Russian heritage, saying she is no longer in a relationship with the Spanish naval commander.
"I definitely know I am not a Russian spy. The last time I checked, I wasn't," she told the British daily.
White said: "I knew he was dealing with the Russian shadow fleet and submarines. But it was a total prohibition of discussing any details at home about this."
Her relationship with the Spanish officer began in October 2024 through the dating app Tinder, shortly after she split up with her ex-husband, a prominent council leader who has visited No 10 Downing Street, according to the report.
According to court documents seen by The Telegraph, he invited her to the social event at Northwood's Warrant Officers' and Senior Rates' mess on Dec. 12, 2024, obtaining a one-day escorted visitor pass to the military base.
"A NATO security investigation was commenced; so, too, was a Spanish security investigation. The UK was not involved in these processes, which resulted in a Spanish decision to suspend [the officer's] national security clearance," a court document said.

Lockheed Martin expands secretive Vectis drone program
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
12:11:22 UTC
21:11:22 KST

- Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works is building four additional Vectis combat drones, bringing the program's total to five aircraft.
- The tailless, stealth-focused drone is designed to fly alongside crewed fighters like the F-35, with a first flight targeted by the end of 2027.
Lockheed Martin is building four more of its newest combat drones, the company announced September 14, doubling down on a program that’s still more than a year away from ever leaving the ground.
The news came from the company’s secretive Skunk Works division, following a major Air Force conference near Washington, D.C., where Skunk Works also unveiled a full-scale model of the aircraft, called Vectis, for the first time.
If you haven’t heard of Vectis yet, here’s the short version: it’s a drone designed to fly into combat alongside piloted fighter jets like the F-35, acting as a kind of robotic wingman. The Air Force calls this category of aircraft a “Collaborative Combat Aircraft,” or CCA, and the idea is straightforward even if the acronym isn’t. Building more fighter jets with pilots inside them is expensive and slow. Building smart, semi-autonomous drones that can fly in formation with those jets, carry weapons or sensors, and take on some of the riskier parts of a mission is, at least in theory, cheaper and faster to scale up.
Lockheed first showed off Vectis a year ago, in September 2025, but the design has changed since then. The version unveiled this week has no tail and a deeply recessed air intake built into the top of the fuselage, both features meant to make the aircraft harder to spot on radar. Ron Fehlen, the vice president and general manager of Skunk Works, told reporters the team is eager to see the pieces coming together.
“The team is extremely excited as these parts start to come together, to actually get the wheels off the ramp by the end of 2027,” Fehlen said.
That end-of-2027 target is when Lockheed expects the first Vectis prototype to actually fly. In the meantime, the company is now building four additional aircraft, bringing the total to five once the original prototype is included. Lockheed hasn’t said publicly what those extra four aircraft will be used for, whether that’s more flight testing, demonstrations for potential buyers, or something else.
For scale, Vectis is about 34 feet long with a 38-foot wingspan, which puts it roughly in the same size class as the Air Force’s MQ-9 Reaper drone in length, with wings about as wide as an F-35’s. It falls into a weight and altitude category the Air Force calls Group 5, meaning it weighs more than 1,320 pounds and is built to fly above 18,000 feet, the same bracket as the two CCA drones already chosen for the Air Force’s first round of the program. Lockheed hasn’t said what weapons Vectis might carry, what kind of engine powers it, or how much each aircraft is expected to cost.
That first round of the CCA program didn’t go to Lockheed. The Air Force picked General Atomics and Anduril Industries instead, and their aircraft, known as the YFQ-42A and YFQ-44A, are being built mainly for air-to-air combat missions. The Air Force has said it eventually wants at least 1,000 of these drones total, built out over several future rounds, and it’s aiming to keep the cost of each aircraft around $20 million, not counting the sensors and other equipment that would go inside. Fehlen said Vectis isn’t necessarily being built for one specific future round of the competition, but that Lockheed sees potential customers well beyond the Air Force, including the Navy and militaries overseas.
One thing Lockheed has been eager to talk about is how quickly the Vectis team has been moving. According to the company, engineers went from an initial sketch to testing a model in a wind tunnel in under two months. The first complete digital design of the aircraft came together in six months, and the team had manufactured its first physical part within eight months of starting the program. Lockheed says that speed comes from manufacturing and design tools built up over years of other Skunk Works projects, not from cutting corners on this one specifically.
Whether Vectis ends up winning a future Air Force contract, getting picked up by the Navy, or drawing interest from an allied country overseas is still an open question. For now, what’s confirmed is that Lockheed is putting real money and staff behind five aircraft instead of one, with a flight test still more than a year away.

Biosphere reserve management regulations under final review
TEHRAN - The judicial and legal committee of the cabinet of ministers is conducting a final review of the executive regulations for biosphere reserves, which will establish the framework for managing the country’s biosphere reserves.
Once approved by the Cabinet, the regulations will establish the specific management framework for the country’s biosphere reserves, IRNA quoted Hamid Zohrabi, an official with the Department of Environment, as saying.
The regulations constitute the country’s first comprehensive framework specifically dedicated to biosphere reserve management. They aim to establish clear management mechanisms, enhance coordination among relevant agencies, and strengthen local community participation, he added.
They also enable the Natural Resources and Watershed Management Organization to establish biosphere reserves, which would contribute to the development of the country’s biodiversity conservation capacities, the official noted.
Referring to the differences between biosphere reserves and protected areas, Zohrabi said that the former seeks to strike a balance between biodiversity conservation and sustainable resource use, as well as promote the socio-economic development of local communities and research activities.
Moreover, it will pave the way for the integrated management of biosphere reserves, the utilization of indigenous knowledge from rural and nomadic communities, and the attraction of targeted investments.
The official went on to say that the implementation of the law will strengthen Iran’s position within the global network of biosphere reserves, and contribute to achieving the goals of the Hangzhou Strategic Action Plan.
Biosphere reserves are territories of outstanding ecological value where people and nature grow harmoniously alongside each other, conserving biological and cultural diversity, advancing sustainable development, and connecting communities across a global network.
Iran, with 14 biosphere reserves, has always been among pioneering member states in the World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
 According to the head of the DOE, Shina Ansari, biosphere reserves cover less than four percent of our national territory, which is not enough, so we are committed to expanding the network by the establishment of four more biosphere reserves.
